docs.title: How to use the Repo Desk
docs.md:
# How to use the Repo Desk

The Repo Desk is one site with two jobs. The **desk** (Market, Funds, Scans, Engine Rules, Docs) shows the nightly market data and the Swing Desk screen. The **Portfolio** tab is the Portfolio Manager: you add your broker files and it tells you, stock by stock and fund by fund, what to keep, sell, reduce or move. Nothing on this site places an order. It gives verdicts and numbers; you place the trade.

## The 5-minute evening routine
1. **Market tab.** Read the regime light (Green, Amber or Red). It sets how much risk a new Swing trade may carry and which setups are allowed. Check the "fresh" chips at the top: if the data is old, the nightly job has not run yet, so wait.
2. **Scans tab.** Read tonight's shortlist. Each line has a trigger (the price that confirms the entry), a limit (the most you will pay) and a stop (where the trade is wrong). A line tagged *over cap* or *room fail* is one the desk itself would not take as listed. Once your accounts are saved, the India tab also shows tonight's OFFICIAL orders sized for each account (how many shares, which limit bound, the level to buy above and tonight's close beside it), worked out each night from your last upload. If an account has not been saved for more than 35 days (you upload each account monthly) it shows as not sized. **Trades by hand.** Between monthly uploads, the Trades tab on the Portfolio page has an *Add a trade by hand* card (buy or sell, any time; the *Taken* button on an official order opens the same card). Type the real shares, price and date; nothing is pre-filled. The trade counts in your positions, open risk, the nightly sizing and the exit alerts until your next upload covers it. After an upload the broker's file wins: a matching trade drops off, a difference is listed with both figures, and a trade the upload should have shown but does not is left out and listed to check. **Paper test tab.** The paper book's capwaived and comparator picks are kept here, apart from your orders: each is tagged with its stream, shows what the live rules say about it, and is never sized against your accounts. The same picks come in their own Telegram note every night, separate from the official orders message.
3. **Portfolio tab, Overview.** The "What to do" card lists what needs action today: stocks to sell, to promote, to harvest, to trim. If it says nothing, do nothing.

## The Portfolio Manager, tab by tab
- **＋ Add files.** Add a tradebook (CSV or Excel) for each account, one at a time. Files are read in your browser. Add a holdings statement (stocks, and separately funds) on the **Data** tab to check that the trades add up to what the broker shows.
- **Overview.** Value, return, the trend line against the Nifty 500, and the "What to do" card.
- **Holdings.** Every holding with its verdict, book (Swing, Legacy or Long-term) and cap size. Click a row for the numbers behind the verdict. Filter by verdict to see only what needs action.
- **Trades.** Every buy and sell, with the book each lot was put in. Near-matches to a shortlist line ask you to confirm "Swing" or "Legacy".
- **Tax.** Gains per person (the exemption and loss set-off belong to one PAN), the estimate for equity and non-equity gains, the Schedule CG working file, and the Harvest and Sell-after cards.
- **Income.** Dividends and interest received.
- **Allocation.** Where the money sits against your target mix, including a look-through into what your funds own.
- **Limits & goals.** Your caps (single company, sector, region, per-person) and the drawdown check.
- **Data.** What is loaded, what is missing, the statement checks and the corrections screen (fix a holding's type, move a transaction to another account).

## What each verdict means, and what you do
The first rule that fires wins, in this order: **Exit, Promote, Harvest, Trim, Keep.**

| Label | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| **Exit** | Closed below its 200-day average or below its last major swing low. | Sell. Tax never delays an Exit. |
| **Promote** | Passes the exit test and is on tonight's Swing shortlist. | Optional: give the lot the shortlist's stop and treat it as a Swing trade. The card says how many shares move in each account under the Swing rules (taken from the oldest lots); the rest stays Legacy. |
| **Harvest** | Passes the exit test, but a loss lot is worth booking: the tax saved beats the cost of selling and buying back by 25%. | Sell the loss lot, buy back the next day or later. Lots and numbers are on the Tax tab. |
| **Trim** | Passes the exit test but is outside your ten strongest stocks, at two weekly checks in a row. | Reduce gradually, weakest first, at most two names at a time and two newly marked a month. Not an order to sell at once. |
| **Keep** | Passes the exit test and is inside the ten-name target. | Nothing. The test keeps watching. |
| **Sell after <date>** | A gain close to its one-year date: waiting for the lower long-term rate saves more than the price risk. | Hold the sale until that date, unless the stock turns Exit. |
| **Replace · Watch** | Funds only, from the published fund scores. | Watch: weakening. Replace: a clearly better fund exists. |
| **No verdict** | Not enough clean price history, or an unadjusted corporate action. | Read the reason on hover. |

Every verdict is written to the verdict log with the price it rested on, and is judged later against rules written down in advance (3, 6 and 12 months).

**Books.** A Swing lot older than 60 sessions (provisional) is shown as Legacy. A sale made within 5 sessions of a close at or below a Swing lot's stop is treated as that lot's exit; any other partial sale of a stock that has Swing lots asks you yes or no on the Trades tab.

## Weekly, monthly, yearly
- **Weekly:** open Overview once. Trim only counts after two weekly checks agree, so checking more often changes nothing.
- **After results season or a big move:** hard refresh, then re-read the Holdings filter for Exit.
- **Before 31 March:** open Tax. Read Harvest (losses worth booking) and Sell after (gains worth waiting for), and the estimate for the year.
- **After filing:** download the Schedule CG working file from Tax; it groups every sale by return section.

## Swing trades in short
A Swing trade starts from a shortlist line. Buy only inside the trigger and limit, put the stop in with the broker, and size by the risk the regime light allows. A volatile stock (ATR above 3% of price) is not bought on a standing order: the entry waits for a confirming close. The Engine Rules tab has the full rules; the change log at the bottom of the page records every change.

## When something looks wrong
- **A chart or return is missing:** the Data tab lists funds with no price history. Hard refresh, then check again; the site fetches fund history through its own service.
- **A change you just heard about is not showing:** the site rebuilds a few minutes after each update. Hard refresh.
- **A stock shows No verdict:** hover it. Usually a split, bonus or demerger the prices have not been adjusted for.
- **A fund is classed wrongly:** use the corrections screen on the Data tab.
- **Numbers disagree with the broker:** add the broker's holdings statement and P&L statement on the Data tab; the check shows the differences line by line.

## What this is not
It is decision support, not tax or investment advice, and it never trades for you. Estimates are before surcharge and cess. Where a rule is a first guess rather than tested, the page says so.

# Swing Desk status: what is confident, what is not, what is left (17 Oct 2026)

Kept current with every change. Confident means built, checked, and I would stand behind it. Not confident means it needs evidence or work before it can be trusted.

## Confident
- Dashboard and nightly India and US data jobs; the regime light (fixed, tested rules).
- Portfolio page accounting (tax, dividends, XIRR, missing-lot detection), checked on real tradebooks.
- Keep/Exit test for held stocks: replayed with split and bonus adjustment; it sorts in the right direction. It is not claimed to beat holding.
- Data plumbing: India prices 2020 to 2025 (1,439 sessions) and index history (1,436 of 1,439) loaded; as-of view passes its leak check; the US replay uses only splits known each night.
- Paper-book mechanics: tested; the official stream reproduces the C-52 replay's trades with identical returns, and adds three the replay's overlap rule or candidate filter left out.
- Process: criteria written before each run, owner marks Adopted, Rejected or Parked.

## Not confident, and how each gets there
1. **Does the US scan have an edge?** One year of data; the result was about zero once one metals rally was removed. Path: the paper book (C-53, logging from 16 Oct) read at 300 picks or 12 months, whichever is later (about Oct 2027); the India baseline (C-54) for the same signal family in days. Confident when the pre-registered pass rule holds on forward data.
2. **Does the pattern layer (pivots, setups, stop widths, room test) earn its place?** No formal evidence; it chokes on volatile stocks (extension, setup geometry, stop width; room binds once stops widen). Path: the three paper-book streams isolate stop width and entry; later the funnel is tested against the plain baseline on six India years. If it cannot beat the baseline, simplify.
3. **Is "swing" the right holding period?** Path: the 20, 60 and 120-session curve in C-54. Days after confirmation.
4. **Does the funnel beat plain momentum?** The India scan is now built and frozen (IND-SCAN-1, 17 Oct, forward log only; pre-registration docs/replay/IND-SCAN-1-PREREG.md). Next: a registered test (C-57) against the C-54 baseline, and a replay once the longer history is in.
5. **India corporate-action list.** Cleared by written rules 17 Oct: 72 of the 76 liquid unexplained breaks (splits, demergers, genuine falls); the 4 left were settled the same day from public sources and are typed in corp-action-overrides-hist.json (one special dividend, two bonuses, one demerger). Factors are rule-derived approximations, not checked against announcements; see docs/replay/INDIA-BREAKS-CLEARED-2026-10-17.md. Path to confidence: check the demerger factors that matter (Siemens, Raymond, ABFRL) against company notices.
6. **Cost assumptions** (India 0.35 / 0.50 / 0.80% round trip). Checked 17 Oct against data/rules/charges.json: statutory plus brokerage is 0.23 to 0.29% round trip for positions of Rs 1 to 5 lakh (0.23 to 0.24% on the cheaper of the two broker schedules in the file, 0.24 to 0.29% on the other), of which 0.20% is STT; small orders on the second schedule cost more (0.36% at Rs 50,000, 0.49% at Rs 25,000) because of the Rs 20 brokerage and DP fee. So the 0.25% statutory part holds for normal sizes. The slippage part (0.10 / 0.25 / 0.55%) is still a guess, not measured; C-54's fit result already holds at double cost. Path: compare fill prices in your tradebooks with the day's VWAP once the files are loaded.
7. **Scan weights 60/25/15.** Signed off, untested. Path: leave frozen; read the paper book's top-10 log; a report-only equal-weight check once the India scan exists. No tuning.
8. **C-54 result: inconclusive (run 17 Oct).** Strong in the fit window (2021 to 2023: +151% against +66% Nifty 500), gave it all back in the holdout (2024 to Sep 2025: +10% against +19%; 2025 alone -20% against a flat index). Momentum is real in some regimes and cyclical with the small-cap cycle, not a free lunch. Path: extend the history back to about 2010 (older NSE file format and a corporate-action source before 2019) so the test sees more cycles.

## Known defects in the existing build
- **US scan was two sessions late (closed).** The free Massive plan posts a day's whole-market file the next evening. FIXED 17 Oct (C-55): the official scan runs the same evening (about 22:45 ET) from the Nasdaq-sourced store; the Massive scan stays as a cross-check. Checked 20 Oct: latest scan is dated 19 Oct, source nasdaq. Listed names only, so every US test states the survivorship bias.
- **Actions minutes (open, watching; one reading a day).** Re-read 19 Oct from billed job time: 1,681 of 2,000 used (the earlier 1,787 counted queue wait). About 12 days to go with roughly 320 left, and the steady weekday cost is about 55 (ticks 26, nightlies 8, ci 15 to 25). Done 19 Oct: ci cancels superseded runs and skips replay notes and STATUS; fund-scores moved from weekly to monthly; the tick's commit step was failing because the dashboard rebuild left unstaged files (fixed); the usage total now comes from a per-run file (data/ops/usage-jobs.json) because the runs list only reaches back 1,000 runs. Done by the owner 19 Oct (cron-job.org): A India `7 14-15,17 * * 1-5` (19:37 IST start, one retry, 22:37 IST alert check); B US evening disabled; C US late and India morning kept at `7,37 0-4 * * 2-6` (it starts the US daily feed, breadth and scan; 1 Nov DST moves them an hour later in UTC and the window still covers it). 13 tick runs a weekday instead of 26, saving about 13 minutes a day. If the reading is still too high, C can start at hour 1 (2 fewer a day). 21 Oct 21:23 IST: GitHub's own billing page shows 1,971 of 2,000 used (our per-run count said about 1,870, so the estimate runs about 5% low); ci is now manual-only (workflow_dispatch). LIFTED 21 Oct 22:53 IST: the owner made the code repo public (unlimited minutes), so ci runs on pushes again and the hold on fetches and backfills is over. 21 Oct: C-80 settled the four open rule questions from the strategy and data (see Engine Rules). ci now also skips docs/**, *.md, site/data and site/pm-data; pushes are batched to one a day until 1 Nov; budget reading 1,860 of 2,000 (140 left, steady weekday about 21 minutes); DONE by the owner 21 Oct: C now `7,37 1-3 * * 2-6` (4 fewer ticks a day, about 17 minutes a weekday). Nothing else in the repo can go below one billed minute per tick. 22 Oct: the owner restored C to `7,37 0-4 * * 2-6` (the repo is public, minutes are unlimited). 22 Oct: the cleaned history was published and the private rules moved to the private repo; Engine Rules copy re-exported at doc rev 226.

## Pending scope of work, in order
**Owner decisions:** whether the Portfolio Manager design doc may appear on the desk (and SCOPE). Decided 17 Oct: US long history from Nasdaq's public API, listed names only (survivorship bias disclosed in every test); no purchase.
**Next builds:** (1) DONE 17 Oct: C-54 run, inconclusive; IND-SCAN-1 built and frozen; US 10-year history loaded from Nasdaq (data/us/hist); (2) DONE 17 Oct: US same-evening scan built and made official from the Nasdaq store (C-55; Massive scan kept as cross-check); India scan and paper book (IND-PAPER-1, C-56) running nightly and shown on the desk Scans tab; (3) DONE 17 Oct: all 76 liquid breaks cleared (72 by rule, 4 by owner answers); (4) cost check with the 2x test; (5) longer India history (2010 to 2019) and re-run; (6) C-57 shape-by-shape test and the formal backtester.
**Calendar, 20 Oct:** scripts no longer name a calendar year (`src/engine/calendar-files.ts` merges every `markets-<year>.json`); the tick alerts from 1 Dec if the next year's file is missing. The 2027 file itself must be added once NSE and NYSE publish their lists. Without it, 2027 holidays would be treated as sessions.
**Backtester module (owner request):** partly built (loader, as-of view, live-exit simulator, manifest and holdout gate, first registered run C-70). Left: standard report on every run, 2010 to 2019 history (after 1 Nov), a US loader. See SCOPE.md, Backtester module.
**Multiple scan strategies (owner request, 20 Oct):** not started; proposed shape and an open question in SCOPE.md. Needs the owner's choice of strategies.
**Portfolio Manager:** verdicts (200 SMA, swing low), relative strength rank, segment tag and the nightly context refresh are built and shown on the Upload and Holdings page. Built 19 Oct: next results date for each held stock (NSE announced board-meeting dates, `site/pm-data/results-next.json`) in the stock's detail row, and a "Results due within 10 sessions" line on the What to do card; information only, no rule change. Built 20 Oct: the Market tab holdings card (see below) and a second source for results dates: NSE's whole-market event calendar, saved nightly by scan-earnings (data/india/scan/results-calendar.json) and merged by build-pm-site (the fresher date wins; disagreements are listed under `differs` in results-next.json). BSE was probed and refuses the runners (Access Denied), so it is not an option. Takes effect from tonight's India scan run. Built 20 Oct (phase 5): the allocation engine (`src/pm/allocation.ts`, settings in `settings/allocation.json`, mapping in `src/pm/assetclass.ts`) and an Allocation tab on the Portfolio page: capital, risk profile (Cautious, Balanced, Aggressive, Custom), horizon in years, optional liquidity buffer and which of the ten asset classes are on give a target per class, set against what is held, with the drift band, the rule behind each number and the single-stock and single-fund limits. Equity share glides continuously with the horizon. Two tests run on every input combination (`test/pm-allocation.test.ts`): targets add to 100% within every cap or a plain message names the clash; a one-notch input change moves targets by a bounded amount. After an external review (20 Oct) three values changed: gold share of non-equity 25% to 20% (the default no longer hits the gold maximum), the drawdown limit is now equity share x 40% assumed bear-market fall instead of a flat figure, and the hybrid fold for balanced advantage, dynamic asset allocation and equity savings counts unhedged equity (40% and 25%). A randomised 20,000-input test was added. Phase 7 part 1 built 20 Oct (`src/pm/swingpools.ts`, `test/pm-swingpools.test.ts`, a Swing pools card on the Allocation tab for a household with two or more accounts): swing capital per account is derived (the household swing target x the account's share of what the household holds), the position cap and the one-stock-one-account rule are checked across accounts, and the card names the account where the next new swing trade would go (already held, then cash, then tax, then fewer positions). (household-specific detail kept in the private repository) Tax routing needs owners assigned to the accounts. Not built: the nightly Swing shortlist does not yet use the account split, open-risk limits are not shown, and the source of capital is one setting, not a per-account record. Per-account allocation built 20 Oct (owner request): every account has its own capital to allocate, risk profile, horizon, buffer, new money, scope and custom weights (saved with the account, see the next entry); the household view is the sum of the accounts' own targets and holdings (`rollUp` in `src/pm/allocation.ts`), and swing capital per account is now the account's own swing target x its own capital, not a share of a household figure. Old single-set inputs are ignored. Phase 7 finished and phase 6 gaps closed 20 Oct. Tonight's swing orders by account (`src/pm/swingorders.ts`, `test/pm-swingorders.test.ts`, card on the Allocation tab for a household): the public nightly plan (trigger, stop, setup from the India scan and paper book) is sized in the browser for each account on that account's own swing capital using the Swing Desk's own sizing (`ntCalc`) and the rules table for today's market light (India VIX above 20 halves risk), with the binding constraint shown per account (one R of risk, 20% position cap, the account's open-risk limit, the household open-risk limit, household position count, a short-term Legacy lot blocking the stock, a setup not allowed on the light) and routed by the existing order (already held, tax, fewer positions, more room). Holdings never leave the browser, so nothing private reaches data/. Open risk needs a stop for each open Swing position: typed once under the card (stored in the browser); until then open risk is understated and the card says so. Not applied there (they need the trade journal): sector pilot sizing, proven-Green 1%, risk halving. Phase 6 gaps: exit loads (`data/rules/exit-loads.json`, typed with evidence; empty because the sandbox cannot reach AMC sites; a fund with no record bought in the last year is flagged to check; known loads count toward cost and those lots sell last); quarterly cap (press 'I acted on' for a class; no new sale suggestion for it that quarter unless drift passes twice the band); slab-rate tax (rate typed per account, kept in the browser; priced into slab-rate lines); fund Replace/Exit sales are wired but switched OFF (`rebalance.fundVerdictSales` false) because the fund-score back-test required by design 9.1 has not run and Exit needs structural data that does not exist yet. New settings values are PROPOSED, for the owner to confirm. [private note kept out of the public repo]  Swing recognition built 20 Oct (owner: a trade can be near a setup without matching it exactly): the nightly India shortlist is now saved (`data/india/shortlist/<date>.json`, from `scripts/save-shortlist.mjs`; line = symbol, setup, stream, trigger, limit, stop, ATR %, desk tags; two nights back-filled from the paper book). A real buy is EXACT (entry session, inside trigger and limit, a calm stock, a line the desk did not tag over cap or room fail): Swing automatically with that line's stop and setup. It is NEAR (up to 3 weekdays later, or up to 2% outside the range; a stock with ATR above 3% may fill up to 5% above the limit, because its entry waits for a confirming close; a line tagged over cap or room fail is always near): proposed on the Data tab, Swing only on the owner's yes, answer saved with the account. Otherwise Legacy. Numbers are approved working values (settings/allocation.json swingMatch; Engine Rules C-76), untested until 40 shortlist nights exist. Two independent reviewers (logic; security and persistence) found 20-odd issues the same day; fixed: volatile entries, rejected paper lines, settings failing open, per-account running open risk and position cap within a night, account rename and delete losing inputs, parallel and stale saves (settings now saved as a per-key patch, one save at a time per account, retry on a lost race), ghost accounts, null body, CI no longer runs for portfolio/ saves. The six gaps the reviewers left were closed the same day (owner: build all and close it): (1) a sale of a stock after a Swing buy is put to the owner ("was this your Swing exit?"); yes moves those units out of the Swing book, the tax view stays oldest-first; (2) a second order of the same stock the same day, or a later add within 12 sessions of a matched buy (the rules add only at the first +1R close, and the 10-session time stop sells a trade with none), is proposed as part of that trade; (3) an exact match above 6% of the account's value is only a near match; (4) sessions skip exchange holidays and count extra sessions (data/calendar); (5) the job now writes data/india/shortlist/index.json (nights it ran, go-live date) and the desk names nights the job missed; (6) passages wrapped in private markers are removed from the published copy of this page (scripts/strip-private.mjs). The owner approved 6% and 12 sessions on 20 Oct; the near-match numbers (3 sessions, 2%, 5%) stay PROVISIONAL, Engine Rules C-76. Swing journal from real trades built 20 Oct (owner request; Engine Rules C-77, Proposed): every buy recognised as Swing (exact, or near and confirmed) becomes a trade, open or closed, grouped by stock and buy date, with its sells from the broker data (plus sales you confirm as your Swing exit). It is scored with the Swing Desk's own maths (`src/engine/journal.ts`): R on the units bought gross of charges, equity on Swing trades only starting from the household's swing capital, risk halving (three losses in a row, or equity 5% below peak), and the Journal Test (20 closed trades over 90 days; expectancy +0.3R, average loss 1.2R, rule breaks 2 or fewer in the last 20, drawdown under 8%). A card on the Allocation tab shows it; halving and the proven-Green 1% feed tonight's order sizes for a household of two or more accounts. You answer Yes or No per closed trade for 'rules followed' (broker data cannot show it); an unanswered trade blocks the Rule breaks test, and proven Green is also blocked while sale or near-match questions are open, sells cannot be explained, or a trade is left out after a split or demerger. Not measured: MAE, MFE, charges, slippage against a planned fill. A trade whose stock had a split, demerger or rename after the buy is left out and named. An independent review the same day found 10 issues; fixed: a stopped-out trade dropping out when the account shrinks, a closed trade offered as the base of an add, mixed units after corporate events, same-day fill order, the answer cap (now 2,000) and wording. Not fixed: the single-account household gets the journal card but no order sizing card. Trades tab built 20 Oct (owner request: all trade history, not only Swing): every buy and sell in the statements for stocks, ETFs and funds (`src/pm/tradehistory.ts`, `test/pm-tradehistory.test.ts`), shown four ways with one set of filters (account, type, book, open or closed, year, search by name): a table with one row per holding that opens to its buys and sells, a monthly timeline, a card per stock, and a chart of realised profit by month with best and worst holdings. Realised gain on each sale is the Tax tab's oldest-first figure, so the two agree. Display only: no rule uses it and nothing new is stored. Units held and the status (Open, Partly sold, Closed) come from the tax replay, so bonuses, splits and demergers do not make a stock look closed; a stock with no buy in the statements (units that arrived by demerger, bonus or grant) is flagged and its cost and first date are unknown; funds the AMFI list cannot match are listed too, from their trades. Each sale's gain follows its own price within a same-day group. An independent review found 8 points the same day; fixed all but: a phone shows the holding table scrolled sideways, and the Account, Book and Last sold columns are not hidden on small screens. Limits: a stock renamed or demerged is shown under the key the statements use, so its history can split across two names; the book shown is where the holding sits now (a stock that is both Swing and Legacy shows both). Trade review built 20 Oct (owner request: learn what went well and what did not): a Review view on the Trades tab (`src/pm/tradereview.ts`, `test/pm-tradereview.test.ts`). For every holding that has been sold it states the result on the units sold against the Nifty 50 index fund over the same days, the 20-session run-up before the buy, the buy against the year's high, the worst dip and best run while held, how much of the best gain was given back, and what the stock did in the 20 sessions after the sale, from the stored split-adjusted daily closes (since April 2021), then lists what went well and what did not and gives a one-word grade (Went well = a profit that kept up with the index; Mixed = a profit behind the index; Did not go well = a loss). Swing trades are also checked against the planned stop (a loss near 1R is as planned; past 1.25R is not) and your rules-followed answer. The Review card follows the account chosen in the side list (one account, one person's accounts, or the household): with more than one account it shows a table with each account and a total row (sold holdings, how many went well, mixed or not, share at a profit, how many beat the Nifty 50, average days held, realised), and the patterns below are for the selection. A card on top states patterns across trades (winners against losers holding days, late entries, giving back gains, selling early, beating the index) only when each group has at least 5 trades. Funds are reviewed only when fund NAVs are switched on. A stock whose history has a split or demerger the stored prices cannot adjust, one with no buy in the statements, or one with no symbol is left out of the entry and exit checks and counted. The wording thresholds (20% run-up, 15% dip, half the gain given back, 15% rise after the sale) are display choices, not trading rules. Commentary only: nothing here changes any rule or any order size. Trade review extended 20 Oct (owner: what went wrong, what a stop would have saved, why I bought): each sold holding now also shows a main issue for a loss (held while falling, chased an entry, the market fell, sold near the low, or unclear; picked from the numbers in that order), a stop-loss what-if (a fixed stop 8%, 10% or 15% under the buy-day close, sold at the first close past it, in rupees on the units sold: money saved on trades that kept falling, and money it would have cost on trades that dipped through the stop and then recovered), and what the market was doing when you bought (change in the 5 and 20 sessions before, distance from the year's high, buy-day volume against the 50-day average, delivery %) with a plain read (chasing a move, breakout, volume-driven, dip buy, or no sign of chasing). The reason in your head is not in the data, so the read is a hint and says so. Stocks bought or sold the same day as others in the account are flagged as one decision. The top card adds the stop what-if totals across all reviewed trades (saved, cost, net) and patterns for volume spikes and main issues. Volume and delivery come from new monthly files (`site/pm-data/volume/`, built from the daily bhavcopy store from January 2021; closed months are not rebuilt) loaded only for the months a review needs. Stop levels and read thresholds are display choices, not rules. Tactical tilt tested 20 Oct (C-74): letting the allocation move with market performance (a monthly trend tilt on equity, international, gold and silver, bounded per profile) did NOT beat static weights in the fit period (Balanced -0.8pp a year, Aggressive -2.0pp after costs); holdout not revealed; no tilt built; re-run on the longer India history after 1 Nov (docs/replay/TACTICAL-TILT-2026-10-20.md). Sector rotation tested 20 Oct (C-75): holding the top two sectors that pass the Swing Desk sector gate, monthly, did NOT beat the Nifty 500 in the fit period (-1.0pp a year after costs, drawdown 36.7% against 18.5%); holdout not revealed; sector and thematic funds stay at 0% in the presets, available only through the Custom profile (docs/replay/SECTOR-ROTATION-2026-10-20.md). Phase 6 built 20 Oct (rebalancing and new-money sizing, `src/pm/rebalance.ts`, `test/pm-rebalance.test.ts`, a Suggested actions card on the Allocation tab): new money is routed first to the classes furthest below target; only a class still above target plus band is sold down, from lots in this order: Exit-verdict names, loss lots, long-term equity (exemption), other long-term, short-term; never the Swing book, locked ELSS or unclassified holdings; each line shows account, units, gain, estimated tax and charges; sales below the minimum trade (Rs 10,000) or costing more than 3% of the sale are skipped (settings/allocation.json, `rebalance`; owner to confirm these two). Not built: exit loads (no data), the one-suggestion-per-class-per-quarter cap (needs a stored decision log), slab-rate tax figures (slab rate not set), hybrid-fund sales, funds' Exit or Replace verdicts as sale triggers. Both rules failed, the holdout was left hidden, no change. Note: docs/replay/HOLDING-PERIOD-INDIA-2026-10-20.md.
Defect found and fixed 19 Oct: the Portfolio Manager's public data (site/pm-data prices, context, regime and the browser modules in site/pm) was rebuilt by every tick but never committed, so the deployed page showed prices from 17 Oct. The tick now commits site/data, site/pm-data and site/pm along with its state files; the dashboard and Portfolio pages refresh from the next successful tick.

Information only, no weight, no verdict change.

- Fund detail also shows the 5-year return against the median of same-segment index funds (Large/Mid/Small Cap against Nifty 50/Midcap 150/Smallcap 250, others Nifty 500 else Nifty 50; at least 3 index funds needed). A fact, not a prediction; closed funds missing on both sides. Built into `site/pm-data/quality.json` by `scripts/build-pm-site.mjs`.

The Portfolio stock panel uses the same card style (`stockCard`). 42 Indian international funds have no fund-page facts (no reliable source found).

**Decision gaps recorded (25 Oct 2026, owner request):** twelve items in docs/SCOPE.md section K (sell-cost box, equity-fund risk strip, stock business facts, fund overlap line, debt-fund credit facts, time-gated tests, international fund facts, hybrid verdicts, goals and household limits, untested items, corrections, what was built). **Move a holding to another account (25 Oct 2026, owner request):** a wrong account or owner on a holding can be fixed in two clicks: "Move to another account…" on the holding's card in the Trades tab (and a "Move…" chip in the Holdings table when one account is selected). # Swing Desk – Engine Rules (Source of Truth)

Oct 3, 2026 · @Owner

## How to use this document

This is the single source of truth for what the Swing Desk decides and why. If the code and this document disagree, this document is right and the code has a bug.

**Rules version:** R-2026.10.9 (R-2026.10.8 plus the removal of the India skipped-days wording, adopted 20 Oct 2026, C-73; R-2026.10.8 was R-2026.10.7 plus the sector zero-return test adopted 17 Oct 2026, C-58; R-2026.10.7 was R-2026.10.6 plus the automatic handling of untyped demergers adopted 15 Oct 2026, C-50; R-2026.10.6 was R-2026.10.5 plus the Legacy exit-test definition adopted 15 Oct 2026, C-41; R-2026.10.5 was the Swing Desk app v9 as of 3 Oct 2026, after two reviews, plus three corrections found in the third review, C-35 to C-37, and the Red setup list, OQ-8. The live Claude desk was patched to v9.1 on 3 Oct 2026 and now follows these rules, except that it counts weekdays and not exchange holidays until the GitHub build adds the calendar, C-39). Every rule change bumps this number and adds a row to the Change log.

**The change rule:**

1. Write the proposed change in the Change log first, with status Proposed, the reason and the evidence that motivates it.
2. Test it (backtest, replay or paper trade) and record the result in the same row.
3. Mark it Adopted, Rejected or Parked. Only Adopted changes edit the rule text above.
4. Change the code, then record the code version in the row, and re-export this document to docs/ENGINE\_RULES.md in the repo in the same commit. The Code and Architecture document is updated in the same step if data, settings or structure changed.

Rejected ideas stay in the log permanently so nobody re-tests them without new evidence.

**Scope:** the rules apply to both markets. Where India and the US differ, the difference is shown in a per-market table and the reason is given. Parameters live in settings files, never inside the code (see the Code and Architecture document). 

**Precedence between documents:** this document wins over every other. The app's Rules tab (the playbook) is the trader-facing manual derived from the current rules version, and the Master Rules document and the scope of work are inputs and plans. If any of them disagree with this document, this document is right and the other one is updated, never the reverse.

## Principles

The desk is built on risk first, momentum second, and as little discretion as possible.

- **Market first.** The regime traffic light decides how much risk is allowed at all. A strong stock in a Red market is still a small position or no position.
- **Leaders in leading sectors.** Money is made in the strongest sectors and the strongest stocks inside them. Weak sectors are not traded.
- **Fixed risk per trade.** Every position is sized from the stop distance so a stop-out costs a fixed fraction of capital.
- **Rules decide, the trader executes.** The tool tells the trader what is allowed. It does not place orders.
- **Data accuracy beats rule cleverness.** A rule fed wrong numbers is worse than a simple rule fed right ones. Every number carries its source and date, and stale data blocks a decision rather than being silently used.
- **Same logic for both markets.** India and the US share one rule set. Differences are parameters, each with a stated reason.
- **Nothing is changed without a log entry.** See the change rule above.

## Regime traffic light

The regime is Green, Yellow or Red, computed on the market benchmark (India: Nifty; US: SPY) and taking the worst of the tests below.

| Test | Rule | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trend | Benchmark above both 50 and 200 SMA and the 50 SMA rising | Green. Above one average and below the other, or 50 SMA not rising: Yellow. Below both: Red |
| Distribution days | 5 or more in the last 25 sessions | Caps the regime at Yellow |
| Breadth | Share of stocks above their 50 SMA below 40% | Caps the regime at Yellow |
| Follow-through day | A confirmed follow-through day after a correction | Lifts Red to Yellow |
| Volatility (India) | India VIX above 20 | Halves the risk per trade |

**Exact definitions (from app v9):**

- **Benchmarks:** India uses Nifty 50 and Nifty 500; US uses SPY and QQQ. Each is read as Green (above 50 and 200 SMA, 50 rising), Mixed (above one average and below the other, or 50 SMA not rising) or Red (below both). The trend level is the lower of the two.
- **Distribution day:** the index closes down 0.2% or more on higher volume than the previous non-skipped session (a skipped day's volume is never the baseline, C-36). A day drops out after 25 sessions, or earlier if the index closes 5% above that day's close. Five or more active days cap the regime at Yellow. The US uses SPY volume with no expiry adjustment.
- **Skipped days:** none, in either market. The engine can skip a flagged day (the skip field on a tracker row), but no day is flagged: every session counts for distribution and follow-through, as in the US. C-72 (20 Oct 2026) tested excluding India's monthly expiry, Muhurat and after-holiday sessions and found no improvement, so the earlier India skip list was dropped (C-73).
- **Follow-through day:** after the index makes a new low, day 1 is the first close above the previous day's high. On day 4 or later, a close up 1.25% or more on higher volume than the previous session is the follow-through day. A new low before that restarts the count. Follow-through is only looked for inside a correction. The correction tracker arms when the benchmark closes 8% or more below its highest close of the last 60 sessions, or when the trend test reads Red (below both its 50 and 200 SMA), whichever comes first; it disarms when the benchmark closes above that 60-session high again. At arming, the low is the lowest low since the 60-session closing high, and day 1 and the day count are worked out from that low over the stored rows, not from the arming day; so a follow-through on the arming day itself is valid, and the rally-low failure test uses that seeded low and is never set above the true low. If a new low forms after arming, it replaces the seeded one and restarts the count. All follow-through state is cleared when the tracker disarms. A follow-through lifts Red to Yellow and nothing else: if the tracker is armed but the trend is Yellow, it is recorded and changes nothing. The 8% and 60 sessions are untested starting values (C-35).
- **Follow-through status:** Active when it happens, Confirmed when breadth goes above 50%, Failed if the index closes below the rally low or breadth has not passed 50% within 10 sessions. Sessions, here and everywhere in these rules, are counted on the market calendar: weekends and exchange holidays are not sessions (C-37). Active or Confirmed lifts Red to Yellow.
- **Breadth:** the share of a stock universe whose close is above its own 50-day average, in percent to one decimal. India: the Nifty 500 (NSE's current list) on stored NSE closes. US: the S&P 500 (the S5FI definition) on Nasdaq's public history. A stock needs 50 sessions of history and is left out (counted as skipped) when any one-day move inside its 50-day window is beyond 22%, which marks an unadjusted split or bonus. Today's list is used for past days, so past breadth carries survivorship bias. Below 40% caps the regime at Yellow.
- **India VIX:** above 20 halves risk per trade.

## Sector ranking

Only sectors that pass the gate are ranked, and only the top four are tradable that week (top two in Yellow).

1. **Gate.** The sector's 3-month return beats the benchmark's 3-month return, the sector's own 3-month return is above zero (C-58), and the sector is above its 50 SMA. In Red mode the 50 SMA test is dropped; the two 3-month tests still apply. A sector that is falling, but falling less than a falling benchmark, does not pass.
2. **Score.** 2 × 3-month return + 1-month return. Highest score ranks first.
3. **Top four** are kept each weekend.
4. **Confirmed or early.** Above the 200 SMA is confirmed (full size). Below it is early (pilot size only).
5. **Persistence.** A sector must appear in the top four on two consecutive weekends before it earns full trust. A new leader (a sector that jumps from outside the top 8 into the top 4 within three weeks) that has not yet persisted may be traded as a pilot only.
6. **Concentration.** Maximum 2 open positions per industry and 3 per sector.

**Data basis.** India sector returns and SMAs come from the official NSE index close file. US sector returns come from stored unadjusted closes. The US 200 SMA is computed from those stored closes, which can sit up to about 1.3% below published dividend-adjusted averages for dividend-paying ETFs. This is expected and is not a data error (see Change log C-14).

## Stock selection

Stocks are only considered inside sectors that rank in the current top group.

**US candidate screen (live in app v9, run weekly):**

| Test | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Pool | Top 10 holdings of each sector ETF in the top group (Yellow: 2 sectors, Green: 4) |
| Trend | Close above 50 and 200 SMA, and 50 SMA above 200 SMA |
| Leads its sector | 1-month return at least equal to its sector ETF's 1-month return |
| Liquidity | Average daily dollar volume of $50 million or more |
| Results | Next results date more than 10 trading days away. Unknown date is flagged, never passed |
| Setup and room | A permitted setup is in place, stop width is within the setup's limit, and there are 3R of room to the 50-day high |
| Freshness | Stock data dated before the screen date is excluded |

A stock is **Ready** when every test passes and **Watch** when trend, liquidity and results pass but no setup, room, stop width or relative strength is in place. The trader still checks the 3-month relative-strength line against SPY on the chart before buying. 

**India stock scan (Chartink, manual until the GitHub build):** the Minervini trend template: close above 150 and 200 SMA, 150 above 200, 200 SMA rising versus a month ago, 50 SMA above 150 and 200, close above 50, at least 30% above the 52-week low and within 25% of the 52-week high, traded value over ₹10 crore a day, price over ₹50, market cap over ₹1,000 crore.

**Known limits:** the US screen uses 50-session highs and lows, not a full year. It reads holdings of the ETFs only, so smaller stocks outside the sector indexes are not found until the whole-market scan is built (Parked item P-1).

**Target rule (not yet built, see Change log C-20):** one trend template for both markets, applied to the whole liquid universe each night, with a relative-strength percentile rank. India and US use the same tests with different liquidity floors.

## Setups and entry calculation

| Id | Setup | Trigger above basis | Limit above trigger | Max stop width | Basis price | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Base breakout | 0.5% | 1% | 8% | Pivot (top of the base) | Stop: low of the last tight area |
| 1ipo | IPO base breakout | 0.5% | 1% | 10% | Pivot (top of the IPO base) | Listed 30 or more sessions ago (no IPO in its first 30 trading days) |
| 2 | Pullback to 20 EMA | 0.2% | 1% | 7% | High of the day that closed at or above the 20 EMA | Stop: pullback low. Skip if the pullback closes below the 50 SMA |
| 3 | Earnings gap | 0.2% | 1.5% | 8% | Gap-day high | Stop: gap-day low. Exempt from the results-date test. Not used in the US |
| 4 | Pullback to 50 SMA | 0.2% | 1% | 6% | High of the holding day | Stop: lowest low of the pullback. Skip if the pullback closes below the 50 SMA |

**Entry calculation (function ntCalc in app v9):**

1. Trigger price = basis price × (1 + trigger %). The basis is the pivot for a breakout or the pullback high for a pullback.
2. Limit price = trigger × (1 + limit %). Orders above the limit are not chased.
3. Stop = the setup's structural stop (US screen: the lowest low of the last 10 sessions). If that stop is closer than 1.5 × ATR(14) below entry, it is widened to entry − 1.5 ATR so ordinary noise does not stop the trade out.
4. Stop width must not exceed the setup's maximum. If it does, the trade is skipped, not resized.
5. Room: distance from entry to the nearest overhead resistance must be at least 3R in both the US and India (India ran at 3R from the start; C-112). A breakout with no overhead resistance passes (in the manual checklist, a resistance level of 0 or at or below the entry means none above).
6. Results: the next results date must be more than 10 trading days away.
7. Size comes from the sizing section below.

Why the markets differ: the room test is now 3R in both markets (C-112). The owner first stated 2R for India on 3 Oct 2026 because of the tax cost of US stocks, but the India scan and paper book always ran at 3R and a 2R trial was not adopted. Setup 3 (earnings gap) is skipped in the US because US results gaps of 20% happen and a stop cannot act overnight (C-25). The 3R test also covers the extra brokerage and slab-rate tax.

## Position sizing and limits per market

Shares = (capital × risk per trade) ÷ (entry − stop), then limited to 20% of capital per position. India VIX above 20 halves the risk per trade.

**India**

| Regime | Setups allowed | Sectors traded | Risk per trade | Max positions | Max open risk (new trades) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Green | 1, 1ipo, 2, 3, 4 | top 4 | 0.5% | 10 | 5% |
| Yellow | 1, 1ipo, 3, 4 | top 2 | 0.5% | 5 | 2.5% |
| Red | 1, 4 | top 4 | 0.25% | 2 | 0.5% |

**US**

| Regime | Setups allowed | Sectors traded | Risk per trade | Max positions | Max open risk (new trades) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Green | 1, 1ipo, 2, 4 | top 4 | 0.5% | 4 | 2% |
| Yellow | 1, 1ipo, 4 | top 2 | 0.5% | 4 | 2% |
| Red | 1, 4 | top 4 | 0.25% | 2 | 0.5% |

Values are copied from LIMITS and LIMITS\_US in app v9. The last column is the maximum total open risk for new trades, because the code compares open risk against capital times this percentage. It is not a position cap; the position cap is 20% of capital (next section). In Red the playbook allows pilots only, and the checklist enforces that, so the setup list for Red is setups 1 and 4 only, in both markets (owner decision 3 Oct 2026, OQ-8 closed; app v9 let Red accept every setup) (C-24, C-38).

A stock scoring Ready on the US screen is still sized by the normal New trade checklist; the screen never sizes a trade.

## Entry mechanics and book rules

These rules were already in app v9 but missing from this document until the 3 Oct 2026 review.

- **Two-part entry:** buy 60% of full size at the trigger. Add the other 40% after a close at +1R and move the stop on all shares to entry. If the first +1R close is already at +2R or higher (a gap), skip the add and sell the third under exit rule 5. Adds do not count toward the daily entry cap.
- **Pilot size:** risk is capped at 0.25% when the sector is a new leader that has not yet persisted, when the stock is a bottom-up leader (3 or more stocks of one industry passing the scans) in a sector that has not persisted, when the sector is below its 200 SMA (early), and in every Red market. A bottom-up leader skips the sector rank, persistence and 200 SMA checks (the industry evidence stands in for them) and trades at pilot size until its sector persists.
- **Red path:** a Red-market trade needs an RS leader (India: top 20% of Nifty 500 on 3- or 6-month return; US: RS line against SPY rising or at a new high) trading above its own 50 SMA, and one of the setups.
- **Entry order type: if ATR is above 3% of price, skip the intraday standing buy order. If the stock closes above the pivot in the top half of its day's range, place a limit buy at that close + 1% the next morning (India: an after-market order, AMO; US: a limit buy) and skip the trade if it does not fill. Never use a market order for a buy. In the trade record, method is amo for this close-confirmed entry and gtt otherwise. The stop is always a standing order placed the same evening as the fill**.
- **Daily cap:** at most two new entries a day, highest RS first.
- **Position cap:** no position above 20% of capital, even if the risk formula says more.
- **Sector rank:** the stock's sector must be in the top 4 (top 2 in Yellow).
- **Legacy book (India long-term holdings):** the exit test is a close below the 200 SMA or below the last major swing low. The last major swing low is the most recent confirmed pivot low on daily closes: a close that is the lowest of the 10 sessions on each side of it, confirmed only after 10 later sessions. The 200 SMA is the mean of the last 200 closes. Closes are first adjusted for splits, bonuses, large dividends, rights and demergers (a typed record that passes the price check first; otherwise a fall of 15% or more across the ex-date is used as the factor, and a smaller one drops the closes before the ex-date, C-44, C-50). The test gives no verdict where an action in the last 300 sessions cannot be adjusted, the latest close is over 7 days old, or fewer than 200 sessions exist and the swing low is not broken; a stock with fewer than 200 sessions that closes below its swing low is still an Exit, labelled as swing-low only (C-41). A passing holding gets a stop just under the higher of the swing low and the 200 SMA, and is trimmed until the drop from price to stop is at most 1% of capital and no holding exceeds 20% of capital. The legacy book has its own 3% open-risk budget, separate from new trades, and the 10-stock maximum is the target for the whole book. Trims sell the oldest lots first (FIFO), so loss lots book a tax loss first. Legacy trailing (copied from the app Rules tab, OQ-7): kept winners follow the week-8 trail rules from day one. Every weekend, raise each legacy stop to the higher of the 10-week average and the last swing low. Exit on a weekly close below the 10-week average (rule 6) and sell a third on a climax (rule 7). Stops never move down. Tighten first, trim second: if the combined give-back is above 3% of capital, first tighten stops to the 10-week-average level; trim only if the book is still above 3% after that, starting with the largest single give-back. The give-back is the combined drop from today's prices to the stops across all kept holdings; a holding whose stop is above its cost puts no capital at risk. The legacy book does not count toward the open-risk cap for new trades, but it counts toward the 10-stock book. Concentration applies to it too: kept holdings count toward 3 per sector and 2 per industry. For a crowded group keep at most three, the strongest on the exit test, and on a tie sell first those whose tax is already covered. 

**Risk halving:** risk per trade halves automatically after three closed new trades in a row below 0R, or while new-trade equity is 5% or more below its peak (that case ends when equity recovers); the three-losses case ends after two winners close. India VIX above 20 halves it again.

**Checklist rules not stated elsewhere:** every trade needs an RS leader (India: top 20% of Nifty 500 on 3- or 6-month return; US: RS line against SPY rising or at a new high). The stop must sit at a chart level, at least 1.5 × ATR away and within the setup's maximum width. Never add to a loser. The checklist is the app's 60-second check, and one failed item means skip.

**Equity basis for the journal tests:** the fresh-money tests, the 8% drawdown test and the 5% halving trigger are computed on new-trade equity only: starting capital plus the profit and loss of closed new trades, as the app's equity curve does. The legacy book is not in these numbers, so a bad week in the legacy holdings cannot fail the system test; track its give-back separately.

**MAE and MFE** are computed from evening closes (the best and worst close, in R), not from intraday highs and lows. A close-based MAE understates how often a stop was nearly hit, so correct it from the chart when closing a trade.

## Exits, journal and review

**Exit rules** (applied in order every evening to every open position; written for India with a broker GTT, the US equivalent is a stop order):

| # | Trigger | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Buy order filled | Same evening place a stop sell for the full quantity at the stop, no limit price |
| 2 | Price hits the stop | The stop sells. Never cancel it or move it lower |
| 3 | Failed breakout: closes back below the pivot within 3 sessions | Sell next morning |
| 4 | Time stop: 10 sessions without a close at +1R | Sell, the capital is idle |
| 5 | A close at +2R or better | Sell one third, move the stop on the rest to entry |
| 6 | Trail, once rule 5 has sold the third (C-68): weeks 1–7 first daily close below the 20 EMA; from week 8 first weekly close below the 10-week average | Sell the rest next morning |
| 7 | Extended, once rule 5 has sold the third: close 20% or more above the 20 EMA, or the biggest up-day of the move after 3+ weeks of gains | Sell another third |
| 8 | Results due within 2 sessions | Gain below 2R: exit. 2R or more: hold with the stop at entry |
| 9 | Regime drops a level | Positions below +1R: stop to today's low or the 10 EMA, whichever is higher. Above +1R keep the stop. No new buys |

Volume tests used by setups: breakout day at least 1.5× the stock's 50-day average volume; IPO base breakout 2×; earnings gap 3×. Setup 3 test (copied from the app Rules tab, OQ-7): a gap of 5% or more on 3× the 50-day average volume on results day, and the results show 25% or more sales or profit growth. Entry is the next day: trigger = gap-day high + 0.2%, limit = trigger + 1.5%. Stop = the gap-day low; skip the trade if the stop is more than 8% away, or if the gap came from a deal, block trade or rumour rather than results. For index distribution and follow-through days, volume only has to exceed the previous session; no session is skipped in either market (C-73).

**India-only mechanics:** skip stocks in the 2%, 5% or 10% price bands and any stock that hit a lower circuit in the last 3 months. After any bonus, split or ex-date, re-place stops at the adjusted price.

**US differences in exits:** the trail is a weekly close below the 10-week average from the start, so winners can run for months and approach the 24-month long-term tax clock. US sells go in before the next US open, and a stop is a stop order, not a GTT. The circuit-band and ASM rules are India only.

**Journal.** Each trade logs date, stock, setup, sector rank, regime, planned entry, fill, slippage, stop, shares, 1R, exit date and price, exit rule, R-multiple, MAE, MFE, whether rules were followed, and a note. Skipped setups are logged with the reason.

**Monthly review and the fresh-money test.** Fresh money is added only after at least 20 closed trades over at least 3 months pass all four tests:

| Test | Pass mark |
| --- | --- |
| Expectancy per trade | +0.3R or better |
| Average loss | 1.2R or smaller |
| Rule breaks | 2 or fewer in the last 20 trades |
| Drawdown from equity peak | Under 8% |

The tests also run per setup. A setup that fails alone is dropped. When all four pass in total, risk per trade may rise to 1% (India Green only; the US stays at 0.5%) and fresh money goes in over three monthly tranches, with the review re-run after each.
