Limits: funds alive today (survivorship), groups from today's categories, four dates a year overlap so the 12-month horizon holds about ten independent years, NAV includes dividends so there is no price-gap split problem. One run. Result goes to data/funds/backtest-swingrules.json. | Run 25 Oct 2026, both tests failed; template not used, thematic trend label reworded | Owner asked 25 Oct 2026 after C-106. Not measured: the swing desk's other rules (regime light, sector ranking, setups with stops), which apply to stocks and to a one-month hold. The stock-level 12-1 momentum baseline was already tested (C-54, inconclusive, strong in 2021 to 2023 and flat in 2024 to 2025), so a separate stock ranking test was not repeated. RESULT (manifest C-107-r1, run 25 Oct 2026, data/funds/backtest-swingrules.json; 476 funds, 43 quarterly dates from Jan 2016). TEST 1, trend template on NAV, 12 months: FAIL. Only 19 dates had 10 or more passing funds (20 needed); the passing funds beat their group on 6 of 19 (32%, bar 60%); mean excess +0.2 points; 1 October dates positive in 2 of 5 counted. It also failed at 3 and 6 months (6 and 7 of 19 dates). TEST 2, Exit against Keep, 6 months: FAIL for thematic funds (12 counted dates, 20 needed; Keep beat Exit on 6, 50%; mean +0.1 points) and for plain equity (17 counted; 8 passed, 47%; mean +0.35). At 12 months Keep beat Exit on 7 of 11 dates for thematic (mean +0.5) and 11 of 16 for equity (mean +0.6), a mild lean towards Keep that is short of the counted-date and 1 October bars. Two weaknesses of the measure, stated: when most funds in a group pass, the median excess of the passing set is about zero by construction and a tie counts as a fail (for example Jan to Oct 2024, when about 300 of 320 funds passed the template); and the bars on counted dates were met on fewer dates than expected. The average gaps are 0.1 to 0.6 points, too small to act on either way. Information only, not decisions: top third of the group by 126-session NAV return beat the group median on 25 of 40 dates at 12 months (63%, mean +0.43 points, 1 October dates 7 of 10) and on 29 of 42 at 6 months (69%, mean +0.36, 8 of 10); it would meet the bars but it was not the registered test, eight variants were looked at, and the effect is about 0.4 points a year, less than a typical cost difference between funds. NAV above the 200-session average and 50-over-200 did not meet the bars at any horizon. Pre-registered use, applied: the template is not used (no uptrend tag, no tie-break). The thematic fund label from the NAV 200-session average and swing low is reworded on screen as a trend flag not shown to predict returns (it already drives no sale). Nothing tuned. The price-return ranking is a lead that needs its own rule before anything uses it. | pending |
| C-108 | 2026-10-25 | Portfolio Manager (fund quality facts, and whether any earns a weight in the score) | Registered before building or running. Owner asked 25 Oct 2026 for fund quality checks and whether they can carry a weight in the score. PART 1, facts, information only: the monthly fund-page fetch (fund-holdings workflow, the page already read for portfolios) also records for each fund its managers with start dates, AUM, benchmark, expense ratio and its history, portfolio turnover, exit-load history and launch date (data/funds/quality.json, a monthly snapshot log data/funds/quality-log.json). The fund detail shows them as facts, with flags only for things that are facts: a lead manager who started less than 12 months ago; a manager, benchmark or exit-load change since the previous monthly snapshot; the expense ratio against the category median. No threshold on AUM or turnover is invented. PART 2, weight in the score, the rule: a factor gets a weight only after a registered test shows it improves the ranking. Cost is the one factor testable now, because the page carries the expense ratio history, so the ratio at past dates is known. TEST (cost): score each plain-equity category at each 1 October for every year in which at least 30 funds have an expense ratio on file within 31 days before the date, using only funds that have one. Variant A = the live FUND-3 score. Variant B = FUND-3 with a cost component: the fund's percentile for lower expense ratio inside its category at weight 0.15 (the C-82 cost weight, not tuned) and the other four components scaled by 0.85. Outcome and bars as C-81: Strong band beats the category median over the next 12 months (Test A), Weak band trails it (Test B), a year counts with at least 10 funds in the band, 60% of counted years, at least 5 counted years. Both variants are reported on the same funds and years. USE, fixed now: B passes A and B = the cost component is added to the live score at 0.15 and the live gate is re-run on it; otherwise the score is unchanged and cost stays a displayed fact (cost still matters: it is the one factor known in advance). The other quality facts (manager tenure, AUM, turnover, benchmark) get weight zero: their history before today is not stored (only current managers are listed, AUM is today's figure), so they cannot be back-tested without hindsight. Each is recorded monthly from now and may be tested after 12 months with a rule registered then, the C-101 method. Limits: funds alive today, expense ratio history may start only a few years back so fewer test years, expense ratio is already inside past NAV returns so adding it counts past cost twice and also predicts future cost. One run. Result goes to data/funds/backtest-cost.json. | Registered; building | Owner asked 25 Oct 2026 after the quality-source probe showed the fund page carries managers, AUM, benchmark, expense ratio history and exit-load history. Not measured: whether manager tenure, size or turnover predicts anything. | pending |
| C-108 result | 2026-10-25 | Portfolio Manager (fund quality facts, cost in the score) | Built and run once, as registered. Facts: the monthly fund-page fetch now records managers with start dates, AUM, benchmark, expense ratio and its change dates, turnover and exit load (data/funds/quality.json, monthly log quality-log.json; 774 funds on the first run); the fund detail shows them with fact flags (lead manager under 12 months, changes since last month). They carry no weight and change no verdict. Cost test: expense history on the fund page starts on 1 Jan 2022 for 310 of 320 funds, so only four test years (2022 to 2025) had 30 or more funds with a ratio on file. The rule needs 5 counted years, so the test is NOT TESTABLE and the score is unchanged: cost gets no weight in it. For the record, over those four years the live score and the cost variant gave the same result (Strong band beat its category median in 2 of 4 years, Weak band trailed in 3 of 4), so nothing suggests cost would have helped, but four years do not meet the bar. Side finding: the page's expense-ratio history has bad values on some days (for one fund 0.01% and 3.83% within a week in May 2026), so any later use needs the monthly AMFI figure, not the daily page value. Retest option: re-run when the history reaches 5 test years (Oct 2027) or when the monthly AMFI TER log (data/funds/ter-log.json) is long enough. Other factors (manager tenure, size, turnover): weight zero, recorded monthly, test after 12 months with a rule registered then. | Done; no weight | Run 25 Oct 2026, data/funds/backtest-cost.json. Not measured: whether cost, tenure, size or turnover improves the ranking. | 7d53587d |
| C-109 | 2026-10-25 | Portfolio Manager (hybrid funds not yet scored: Conservative Hybrid and Balanced Hybrid) | Registered before running, approved by the owner on 25 Oct 2026. Question: does the C-82 risk-aware score (3-year return 30, consistency 20, return per unit of volatility 20, worst fall 15; cost left out because no expense ratio exists at past dates, as in C-94 and C-103) rank Conservative Hybrid and Balanced Hybrid funds in the right order inside their own category? Funds: Direct Growth plans in those two AMFI categories, each category its own group, a group needing at least 5 funds with a 3-year record. Method as C-105 (rank correlation, so every fund counts): each 1 Oct, 2015 to 2025, scores use NAVs up to that date only; outcome = next-12-month NAV return minus the median of the fund's own group; the year's Spearman correlation between score and outcome, funds of both categories pooled; a year counts when at least 10 funds are scored. Pass rule fixed in advance: the correlation is above zero in at least 60% of counted years, there are at least 5 counted years, and the mean correlation is above zero. If fewer than 5 years count the result is 'not testable' and nothing changes. If it passes: these two categories get a score band and a Keep or Watch verdict with Replace off, as the other hybrid categories have; if it fails or is not testable they stay unscored. Arbitrage funds are left out on purpose (near-identical hedged holdings, so a score would only rank cost). The result goes to data/funds/backtest-hybrid.json; the live gate and every current score are untouched. | Run 25 Oct 2026: PASS | data/funds/backtest-hybrid.json: 10 counted years (2016 to 2025), 7 positive (70%), mean rank correlation +0.102; three years negative (2017, 2018, 2020). Adopted: Conservative Hybrid and Balanced Hybrid are now scored, Keep or Watch only, Replace off. The effect is small. Not measured: Arbitrage funds (left out on purpose). | adopted 25 Oct 2026 |
| C-110 | 2026-10-28 | Portfolio Manager (index funds: does the gap to the same-index median persist?) | Registered before running, owner said "go" on 28 Oct 2026. Question: C-98 could not test the index-fund bands (Leads, In line, Lags) because each index has too few funds for 5 in a band. Same question, asked as C-105 and C-109 did so every fund counts. Funds: Direct Growth index funds (not ETFs, not fund-of-funds) whose name gives a domestic equity index through indexKey (gold, silver and foreign indices left out); the group is the index. Score: the band's own measure, the 3-year return gap to the median of the same-index group on each 1 Oct from 2015 to 2025, using NAVs up to that date only (a group needs at least 3 funds with a 3-year record, as INDEX_SETTINGS). Outcome: next-12-month NAV return minus the median of the fund's own index group. Statistic: the year's Spearman correlation between score and outcome, all groups pooled; a year counts when at least 10 funds are scored. Pass rule fixed in advance: the correlation is above zero in at least 60% of counted years, there are at least 5 counted years, and the mean correlation is above zero. If fewer than 5 years count it is 'not testable' and nothing changes. If it passes: the existing Leads, In line and Lags band is shown for index funds as Keep for In line and Leads and Watch for Lags (Replace stays off, nothing is sold by it), with the sure saving from the lower expense ratio next to it; if it fails or is not testable the band stays information only. Disclosure: index funds on the same index hold the same stocks, so the gap is cost plus tracking difference, which persist by construction; a pass is expected and shows the band is not noise, it does not show any fund will beat its index. The result goes to data/funds/backtest-indexrank.json; the live gate and every current score are untouched. | Run 28 Oct 2026: PASS. Ten counted years (2016 to 2025; 2015 had no group of 3), the correlation was above zero in all ten (100%), mean 0.487, lowest 0.23 (2025), highest 0.76 (2016). Funds scored per year 13 to 49 in 3 to 13 index groups, so each year is small; years overlap (12-month outcomes from yearly dates). Read as the disclosure says: the gap is cost plus tracking difference, which persists; it shows the band is not noise, not that a fund will beat its index. Action: band shown as Keep (In line, Leads) / Watch (Lags), Replace stays off. | scripts/fund-index-rankcorr.mjs, workflow fund-index-rankcorr-test, data/funds/backtest-indexrank.json | passed |
| C-111 | 2026-10-30 | Portfolio Manager (phase 9: ledger folded into the nightly shortlist) | Plumbing, no rule change. Registered before building, owner said "go" on 30 Oct 2026. Tonight's Swing orders are already sized and routed by account in the Portfolio page (phase 7: sizeOrders, with the one-R, 20% position, account and household open-risk limits, position count, the two-new-names-a-night limit and the setup allowed on the light). Phase 9 runs that same sizing every night without opening the page. The page's input assembly (swing capital from the allocation resolver, open risk and missing stops, blocked names, the journal and its proven-Green and risk-halving state, short-term gains for routing) moved into one shared module in src/pm (orderinputs.ts), used by both the page and a new nightly script, so there is one implementation. The script (scripts/sized-shortlist.mjs, in the india-stocks workflow after the scan and the shortlist save) reads the saved accounts from the private repo (portfolio/accounts, with their settings and answers), the same candidates the page uses (the scan's Ready list plus the paper book's new orders) and the day's market light and VIX, and writes portfolio/book/shortlist-sized-latest.json in the private repo. Nothing is added to the public shortlist files (data/india/shortlist): they are the forward-test log and what C-76 matching reads, and stay as they are. No holding, capital or account detail goes under data/. Stale ledger (design section 1.1): when an account's last save is older than swingPools.ledgerMaxAgeDays (35 days, set by the owner on 30 Oct 2026 because accounts are uploaded monthly and edited on the Portfolio tab in between; in settings/allocation.json), that account's lines are marked unsized with a reason and the file carries a banner; old capital is never used silently. A missing market light sizes nothing, as on the page. The Scans tab (India) shows the file read-only behind Cloudflare Access (/api/portfolio?view=sized); one Telegram message a night (owner asked, 30 Oct 2026) lists the orders placed by account and quantity, then each line nobody can take with its reason, and names any stale account or a missing market light; it is sent again only if its text changes (state in portfolio/book/sized-state.json). No threshold, size, risk or routing rule changes. | Interim: built 30 Oct 2026 | Owner asked to fold the ledger into the nightly shortlist (design section 13, phase 9); prerequisite met, the shortlist is saved nightly since 16 Oct 2026. Tests: test/pm-orderinputs.test.ts (13 tests, with the Telegram text: candidates, names, stale limit at the boundary, capital from each account's own target, typed stops as open risk, a short-term Legacy lot blocking the same stock, overlay equal to the sized lines when nothing is stale, a stale account blanked while the other keeps its size, no light sizes nothing, the route needs a sign-in); the existing sizing tests pass unchanged; 574 tests pass. Smoke run on two invented accounts: one stale, one current, red light, as expected. Not yet seen on a real night: the workflow has not run with the private repo attached since this was built. ledgerMaxAgeDays = 35 follows the owner's monthly upload habit; the save date also moves when only settings are saved, so it can understate how old the trades are. scripts/holding-alerts.mjs passed no shortlist or swing answers to the pipeline, so its book labels read Legacy for every stock; fixed in the same change (it now loads the same public inputs, scripts/pm-nightly-lib.mjs, and passes the account's swing answers and type fixes), so its book names now match the page; Exit verdicts do not depend on books and are unchanged. Not measured: whether sizing at night rather than at upload changes any decision taken. | built 30 Oct 2026 |
| C-112 | 2026-10-30 | Entry (room test, India) | Doc correction, no code change. Owner asked to check whether India's room test is 2R (rules text, C-5) or 3R (code). Found: the India scan inherits roomR 3 from the US settings and the India paper book imports the same constant, so India has run at 3R since it went live; scripts/india-scan.mjs also uses 3. Checked against the saved C-64 replay (live exits, width within cap): room 3R or more n=27, +0.73R; 2R to 3R n=52, +0.10R (error ±0.23); under 2R n=377, +0.06R. Rule at 3R n=40, +0.47R; at 2R n=92, +0.26R. Neither is proven (the replay's own test needs 100 trades and a 0.15R gap), and nothing supports lowering the bar. Owner said ok on 30 Oct 2026: rules text corrected to 3R in both markets under C-79 (what ran). Frozen scan and forward-test clock untouched. A 2R trial would need its own registered test. | Adopted (doc fix) | Aligns the written rule with what has always run | docs only |
| C-113 | 2026-10-30 | Portfolio Manager (official and paper-test orders kept apart) | Plumbing, no rule change. Registered before building; owner said "go" on 30 Oct 2026. (1) The sized card on the Scans tab and the nightly Telegram order message carry OFFICIAL candidates only (the scan's Ready list and the paper book's official stream). (2) The paper book's capwaived and comparator picks move to a new Paper test tab (together with the existing Paper book tables, which leave the Scans page; India and US toggle) and a separate nightly Telegram note, sent every night, each pick tagged with its stream; the note says it is not for placing. Paper picks are never sized against real accounts and never use real open-risk room; the tab shows the live rules' verdict for each (for example the stop-width skip). Capwaived is entered at a buy-above trigger; comparator is entered at the next close after its signal. (3) "Buy at" is renamed "Buy above" and shows the last close and the gap beside it. Out of scope, next as C-114: a Taken mark so that only trades the owner confirms count as open risk. | Adopted (plumbing) | Stops paper-test picks reading as buy orders | app, nightly job |
| C-114 | 2026-10-30 | Portfolio Manager (trades added by hand, Taken mark) | Plumbing, no rule change. Registered before building; owner answers on 30 Oct 2026. Between monthly uploads the owner can add a trade by hand to an account (buy or sell, any time) and mark an official order as taken (the same form, opened from the order). The owner types the actual quantity, price and date; nothing is pre-filled. Hand-added trades count in the account's positions, open risk, position count and 20% cap, in the page and in the nightly sizing, and the nightly exit alerts watch them. Reconciliation on the next upload, worked out each time and never trusted over the broker: a hand-added trade with the same stock, side and date (one day either way) and the same total quantity as the broker's trades is matched and dropped, and a price that differs by more than 0.5% is listed as a difference; a different quantity is listed as a difference and the broker's figure wins; a hand-added trade dated on or before the upload's last trade with no match is left out of every calculation and listed to check. A separate last-upload date (not the last-save date, which moves on every settings save) now drives the 35-day stale check, so hand-added trades do not make an old ledger look fresh. Paper-test picks cannot be marked. | Adopted (plumbing) | Open risk and position slots stay true between uploads | app, nightly job |
| C-115 | 2026-10-31 | Portfolio Manager (tax class of Equity Savings funds) | Tax rule change, registered before building; owner asked for it on 31 Oct 2026. Until now every Equity Savings fund was taxed on the cautious hybrid rule (35% to 65% equity: 24 months, 12.5%, short-term at slab). The test in the tax law is whether the fund keeps at least 65% of its money in equity and arbitrage; HSBC's tax note says equity savings funds are taxed as equity funds when they keep 65% in equity and arbitrage. New: an Equity Savings fund is taxed as an equity fund (12 months, 12.5% on gains above the yearly exemption, short-term 20%) when its own stated minimum equity is 65% or more (the eqMin field in data/funds/mix-auto.json, read from the fund's public page: 21 of the 22 funds in the data say 65). When the stated minimum is below 65% (one fund in the data, Axis) or is not known, the fund stays on the cautious hybrid rule. Confidence stays Medium: the minimum is the fund's mandate, not a measured share, and comes from a public page, not the scheme document. The asset class stays Hybrid. Tax figures stay estimates before surcharge and cess. | Adopted | Most Equity Savings funds are taxed as equity funds; the old rule overstated the tax on them | app, nightly job |
| C-116 | 2026-10-31 | Backtester data (India 2010 to 2019; US survivorship label) | Data only, no rule change. Registered before loading; owner accepted on 31 Oct 2026 (about 80 MB more in git) and chose to label the US bias and go ahead. (1) India: NSE's old daily file (cmDDMONYYYYbhav.csv.zip) is read for 2010 to 2019 into data/india/bhav-hist in the same shape as the 2020 on files (delivery share null); a probe on 31 Oct 2026 showed every session date tried answers from the runner. (2) NSE's corporate-action list for 2010 to 2018 is fetched into its own file (corp-actions-history-pre2019.json) and joined to the existing 2019 on history only after a check that splits and bonuses resolve. (3) US: data/us/hist holds 2,279 symbols from 16 Oct 2016 and every one is still trading, so no delisted names exist in it; every US backtest result must carry the label survivor-biased upward, with the bias estimated where it can be. Existing registered tests keep their own data fingerprints. No scan, setup, exit, sizing or regime rule changes. | Adopted (data) | Longer India history gives later tests the power the 2021 to 2026 window could not; the US label stops survivor bias being read as edge | backtester, data jobs |
| C-117 | 2026-10-31 | Backtester (standard report) | Output tooling, no rule change (src/backtest/report.ts, test/backtest-report.test.ts). The code was written before this row was registered; registered now, before it is committed or used. Every registered test can now print the same report from its list of picks: pick quality at 20, 60 and 120 sessions on the same picks (mean and median net return, mean excess over the equal-weight market, hit rate, 90% block-bootstrap interval of the excess); the result without the single best group; splits by entry year, regime and group (thin cells flagged); how sharply a parameter's result peaks across the values tried; and the caveats the run must carry (US survivor bias, unadjusted prices, sweep size). Nothing in the live engine reads it. | Adopted (tooling) | Every test answers the same questions the same way, so results compare and caveats cannot be left out | backtester |

## Open questions and parked ideas

| ID | Item | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OQ-1 | Copy exact definitions into this document | Closed 3 Oct 2026 for regime, setups and limits. Chartink field names for the India scans stay in the app Rules tab |
| OQ-2 | Why setup 3 is skipped in the US, and the 3R against 2R room test | Closed 3 Oct 2026 (C-25) |
| OQ-3 | Red mode allows the same setups and sector count as Green in app v9, with only risk and position limits cut. Test whether that is right | Closed as Interim 3 Oct 2026 (C-24); backtest in build phase 6 to confirm |
| OQ-4 | Backfill early decisions | Closed 3 Oct 2026. No earlier record exists; rows C-1 to C-6 are logged as design choices |
| OQ-5 | Define how a rules version number and a backtest result attach to a change | Defined 3 Oct 2026 (build phase 6 builds it). Each change-log row records the rules version before and after, the commit that implements it, and a backtest id. A backtest id is a folder data/backtests/\<C-id>/ holding the settings used, the fixture window and the result summary, plus the rules version and the commit SHA the run used, produced by a script that refuses to run when the working tree has uncommitted changes |
| OQ-6 | India stock EMAs are stale for some holdings (the Dhan technical page did not refresh) and two prices came from an earlier run, as flagged in the 1 Oct feed | Open, build phase 1 data checks. This is a fault of the old Dhan source: once phase 1 computes EMAs from stored closes it closes by construction |
| P-1 | Catch smaller stocks outside sector indexes through a whole-market scan | Parked, build phase 4 (C-20) |
| P-2 | Daily screen refresh | Parked until the move off Claude (C-19) |
| P-3 | Ideas from the Master Rules document not yet adopted | Parked, see scope of work (C-18) |
| OQ-7 | Copy the legacy-book trailing rule and the setup 3 numbers' wording from the app Rules tab into this document | Closed 3 Oct 2026: legacy trailing and setup 3 wording copied into this document |
| OQ-8 | Code disagrees with the rule: LIMITS in app v9 lets Red accept every setup, but the rule (C-24) is pilots only. Change LIMITS in v10 so the first engine test asserts the rule, not the code | Closed 3 Oct 2026 by owner decision: Red allows setups 1 and 4 only, in both markets (C-38). Built in the engine repo |

## Proposed improvements (not yet rules)

From a strategy review on 3 Oct 2026. All are Proposed: none is a rule until it is tested on the desk's own data and logged as Adopted. The principle behind the list is to improve the ranking among qualifying setups, not to add filters, because each new filter cuts the number of trades the journal needs to reach 20 closed trades.

| # | Idea | Assessment | Needs | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Rank sectors on 6-month and 3-month relative return and use 1-month only as a gate or tie-break; rank stock RS on a 6-month window excluding the last two weeks | Settled in review: one-month reversal is a single-stock effect, and industry momentum has been reported to continue over one month (Moskowitz and Grinblatt). So the current sector score (2 × 3M + 1M) stays as the rule and is the baseline. The 6M + 3M ranking is the challenger, to be tested against it. For stock RS, excluding the last two weeks still has support and is a challenger too | Whole-market closes, backtest | Baseline kept. Challenger waits for backtest (phase 6) |
| 2 | Rank industry groups by breadth (share of stocks above the 50 SMA, median RS percentile) instead of cap-weighted indices | Sound. Index leaders can be one or two heavy stocks, and past winners came from groups with no index. Depends on the whole-market store | C-20 store | Proposed |
| 3 | Build the whole-market universe before more work on the ETF-holdings screen | Agree. It is already C-20. A US universe source is not chosen yet | Source decision | Proposed |
| 4 | Quantify base quality: 10-day range divided by ATR below about 2, weekly closes within 3% over 3 weeks, up-day volume above down-day volume over 50 sessions | Useful to make the base test objective. Record the numbers on every candidate first and filter only if the journal shows they earn it | Whole-market data | Proposed |
| 5 | Prefer earnings acceleration (growth rising over 2 or 3 quarters) over a growth level | Plausible. Needs a reliable fundamentals source, which is a data-accuracy risk like the others | Fundamentals source | Parked |
| 6 | Rank by closeness to the 52-week high within the existing 25% rule | Cheap tie-break. Log it | Whole-market data | Proposed |
| 7 | A fixed, pre-registered candidate score (RS percentile, industry breadth, base tightness, distance to pivot, volume ratio, earnings acceleration) used when there are more candidates than slots | Good discipline. Record every factor on each candidate from day one, fix the weights before using them, and review after 20 trades | Candidate scan, journal fields | Proposed |
| 8 | Correlation guard: at most 50% of open risk in sectors whose 3-month returns correlate above 0.8 | The numbers 50% and 0.8 are untested guesses. The per-sector cap does not catch a single theme spread across sectors, so the idea is worth testing | Return history | Proposed |
| 9 | Score the base shape of shortlisted stocks only: fit a curve to a cup, measure flatness for a flat base, count shrinking pullbacks and volume for a contraction pattern, and show a small chart with the fit and a score | Practical because the shortlist is only 10 to 30 stocks a night. Patterns are loose descriptions, so a fit only approximates them and the thresholds are our choice. Record the scores only. Compare them with the owner's own yes or no on about 20 past charts (for example the Kaynes and PSU bank moves) before they change what is shown or filtered. Extends idea 4 | Whole-market daily prices, 20 labelled charts | Proposed, build phase 4 |

The review also says a well-run breakout system wins about 40 to 45% of trades and that most of the gap between a weak and a strong system comes from exits, sizing and regime discipline. I have not verified that figure; treat it as a reminder that ranking changes are marginal against the exit rules.

# Swing Desk – Code and Architecture (Source of Truth)

2026-10-03 · @Owner

## Purpose and how the two documents relate

This document says how the Swing Desk is built so a new engineer or an AI coding tool can run, fix and extend it without asking the original author. The companion Engine Rules document says what the desk decides and why. Rules change only through that document's Change log; this document describes the machinery that carries them out.

**Code version:** app v9.1 on Claude Artifacts (3 Oct 2026), patched from v9 to follow Engine Rules R-2026.10.5 (the repo's engine follows the version in `RULES_VERSION`, currently R-2026.10.9). The GitHub build has started in the private repo bpishigh/Swing_desk (phase 0: scaffold, fixtures, source test, Telegram alert, and a TypeScript engine replayed against v9; engine commit b6ae0f6, 3 Oct 2026). The live desk is v9.1 and still fed by the Claude scheduled tasks, so sections marked Target describe the intended design, not what runs.

**Reading order for a newcomer:** this section, the system map, data flow, schema, then the runbook. Read the Engine Rules before changing any calculation.

**Hard rules for anyone changing the code:**

1. No rule value is written in code. It comes from a settings file or table named in the Settings section. (Applies to the rewrite; app v9 still keeps them in constants.)
2. Every number shown to the trader carries a source and an as-of date. Missing or stale data is shown as missing, never filled in.
3. A change that alters a decision is logged in the Engine Rules Change log first.
4. In the Claude runtime, never retry or route around a 403 or 407 from the organisation proxy. On a GitHub runner, a 403 from a source such as NSE comes from the source itself: the right first response is standard browser headers and a session cookie on the first request, logged. Evasion such as rotating addresses or ignoring a site's stated terms is never acceptable. Record every block in the data quirks list.

## System map

Today the desk is one self-contained HTML app with a built-in database, filled by three scheduled Claude tasks. The target moves the fill and the app off Claude.

| Part | Today (app v9) | Target (GitHub build) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App | Single HTML file published as a Claude Artifact (swing-desk.html), rules and screens in one script | Static app on GitHub Pages, one rules module shared by India and US |
| Database | Artifact built-in database, collections listed in the Schema section | JSON files committed to the repo by the nightly job; where trades and the journal live depends on decision 3 below (browser storage is the weakest option) |
| India data fill | Claude task, nightly 21:40 IST weekdays, and morning 07:20 IST Tue–Sat | GitHub Actions script, nightly |
| US data fill | Same morning task; US sector pages, TipRanks SMAs, stored closes | GitHub Actions script, nightly, from verified sources only |
| US stock screen | Claude task, Saturday 08:41 IST, writes the us_screen collection | Same script as the daily scan, run nightly |
| Alerts | None | Telegram or ntfy message after each run and on failures |
| Checks | Manual look at stamps | Automated data-health checks that block a stale run from reaching the app |

**Scheduled tasks today:**

| Task | Id | Schedule | Job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| India nightly | trig_01PmtKhLn7Y14j5QRP791DMC | 21:40 IST, weekdays | Fill India feed and sector closes |
| Morning | trig_01LXdn6TvN5LNpFeAcdQvcGd | 07:20 IST, Tue–Sat | Fill US feed, compute returns and 200 SMAs from stored closes, top up history (max 2 gaps a run). Never uses an API key |
| US weekly screen | trig_01GLFkAY7uPtSXawEcXvAJVH | Saturday 08:41 IST, automatic approval | Build the us_screen document for the sectors in the top group |

The three task prompts are the code of today's data fill. They live inside the scheduled tasks and are not yet copied into this document or a repo, so export them with the fixtures (decision 9) before anything is changed. The Claude app, its database and the tasks are the only runtime. Decided 3 Oct 2026: app v9 stays the live desk on Claude while the GitHub build is made in a private repo, and the two run in parallel until the new data matches (scope of work, phases 1 and 2). If the Claude account or tasks stop, the data stops filling; that dependence is the main reason for the GitHub build.

## Data flow and schedule

**India, each weekday evening (21:40 IST):**

1. Download the official NSE index close file for the day (ind_close_all_DDMMYYYY.csv). Quirk seen on 3 Oct 2026: NSE's whole-market file (sec_bhavdata_full_DDMMYYYY.csv) can carry the previous session's data under a holiday's file name (the 02 Oct file held 01 Oct data), so the engine always reads the date inside the file and never trusts the filename.
2. Append the closes to the idx_closes history, then compute each sector's SMAs and 1- and 3-month returns from that history.
3. Write the feed document (collection feed, doc latest) and the dated tracker row (tracker).
4. The app reads feed and tracker on load and computes the regime under the Engine Rules. Breadth and similar regime inputs are typed in by the trader today (decision 5).

**US, each morning (07:20 IST, Tue–Sat, after the US close):**

1. Read sector ETF and SPY closes from the StockAnalysis pages (latest 50 rows).
2. Merge the rows into the stored closes document (us_feed_hist, doc closes), keyed by date. Existing dates are never overwritten.
3. Compute 1- and 3-month returns for every sector and for SPY from stored closes. Compute the 200 SMA from stored closes where 200 dates exist; otherwise use the TipRanks value and mark sma200Src.
4. Top up history from Yahoo date-windowed pages for at most 2 tickers with gaps, and stop on any HTTP 429.
5. Write us_feed (doc latest) with the date of the data, flags and the fetch time. A run that cannot confirm today's date writes a flag and leaves the previous values.

**US stock screen, Saturday 08:41 IST:** read the top-group sector ETFs from us_feed, pull each ETF's top 10 holdings, fetch each stock's recent history, compute the metrics listed in the Schema section, and write us_screen (doc latest).

**Target schedule (GitHub Actions):** India after the NSE file is published, US after the US close, whole-market scan nightly, each run followed by data-health checks and an alert.

## Data sources, checks and known quirks

Data accuracy has been the main failure of the desk, more than strategy. Each source below has a status, and a source may only feed a decision while its status is Used.

| Source | Used for | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NSE official index close file | India sector closes, SMAs, returns | Used | Complete and dated. Primary India source |
| StockAnalysis ETF pages | US sector ETF and SPY closes (50 rows) | Used | Latest 50 rows only, so history must be stored |
| Stored closes (us_feed_hist/closes) | US returns and 200 SMA | Used | Unadjusted closes, SPY dates as the calendar. Source of truth for US averages |
| TipRanks | US 50 and 200 SMA where no stored history | Interim | Stamps went stale; dividend-adjusted so 200 SMA runs up to about 1.3% lower than computed |
| Yahoo history, date-windowed pages | Top-up of stored closes | Parked | Complete rows but 9 of 32 requests returned 429. Slow top-up only |
| Yahoo full-page history | none | Rejected | Truncated and gappy when read through the Claude fetch tool. Re-test from GitHub (phase 0) |
| Yahoo chart API | none | Rejected | Blocked for the Claude fetch tool by robots rules, not necessarily by the source. Re-test from GitHub (phase 0) |
| Alpha Vantage | none | Rejected | 25 requests a day and a burst limit; owner said not to use the key. PROPOSED (owner decision, 3 Oct 2026, third review): the first probe showed Yahoo 429 and Stooq 403 from GitHub's servers, so the keyless US plan may not hold. The seven-day test now also probes free-tier keyed EOD APIs (Tiingo, Polygon, EODHD) and Yahoo with the cookie and crumb handshake; each key lives only in a GitHub secret and its probe is skipped when absent. The Alpha Vantage key stays unused. Owner approved Tiingo first, with Massive or EODHD as backup, and FRED for VIX, as a logged exception (3 Oct 2026); adoption for production waits on the test (history depth and cross-check) |
| ETF Database averages | none | Rejected | Values unreliable |
| Upstox and Dhan pages | India stock prices, volume, averages and EMAs for the held stocks | Used, with known gaps | The Dhan technical page was stale for a number of the held stocks on 1 Oct (Engine Rules OQ-6). To be replaced by averages computed from stored closes |
| StockAnalysis holdings, history and statistics | US screen: ETF holdings, stock history, 200 SMA, 52-week change, next results date | Used | The stock 200 SMA is the figure the page publishes, not computed here, and whether it is dividend-adjusted is not recorded. Results dates may be missing and are then flagged |
| TradingView and Chartink scans (manual) | Breadth, RS rank, trend template and volume scans | Manual | Run and typed in by the trader. The target replaces these with the whole-market store |

**Checks the pipeline must enforce (target; today partly manual):**

- Every stored value has a source name and an as-of date.
- A date earlier than the previous run's is a failed run, not new data.
- Closes must be unadjusted and must not jump more than a set percentage in a day without a corporate-action note (splits and bonuses corrupt averages otherwise).
- A computed SMA needs the full window of stored dates. Fewer means missing, not approximate.
- A run with a stale or missing source writes a flag and keeps the old values; it never writes zeros.

**Known quirks:**

- Computed 200 SMA differs from published figures by up to about 1.3% for dividend-paying ETFs. This is expected (Engine Rules C-14).
- In the Claude runtime a 403 or 407 means the organisation proxy blocks that site; do not retry or route around it. On GitHub, treat a 403 as the source's own response and follow hard rule 4.
- A 429 means the source is rate limiting. The response asks not to refetch; stop and move on.
- Summaries of fetched pages can report wrong row counts. Count rows in the stored data, not in the summary.
- GitHub servers may be blocked by NSE or Yahoo. None of the target data sources has been tested from GitHub yet; do this first in build phase 0.

## Data schema

The app database is a set of collections of documents keyed by id. In the US market the app adds the prefix us_ to the collections marked in the last column; India uses the bare name. Writes to an existing document need the document's version (if_version), or they are rejected.

| Collection | Document id | Holds | US prefix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| settings | main (India), us | capital, startCapital | document per market |
| tracker | date YYYY-MM-DD | daily benchmark row: close, high, low, volume, sma50, sma200, and b (breadth and related inputs); distribution and follow-through are computed from these rows | yes |
| regime | date | saved regime inputs: n50, n500 (green, mixed or red), dist, breadth, ftd, expiry. Empty today; the regime is computed from tracker rows | yes |
| sectors | weekend date | weekly sector ranking: mode, nifty {m1, m3}, rows[] each with name, rank, score, m1, m3, above50, above200, pass | yes |
| feed | latest | latest data fill: bench, date, fetchedAt, flags, sectors (19 India, 14 US), stocks (India stocks only) | yes |
| feed_hist | date (India); closes (US) | India: one snapshot per day with bench, sectors, stocks. US: the stored closes used to compute returns and averages | yes |
| trades | trade id | planned, open and closed trades (fields below). Empty today | yes |
| logs | log id | skipped setups (type skip) and no-trade weeks (type notrade) with date, reason and outcome. Empty today | yes |
| legacy | h01, h02 and so on | existing long-term holdings under the exit test: stock, symbol, isin, sector, industry, qty, avg, status, bucket, tax, order. India only | no |
| overrides | stock symbol | manual stand-in values: date, savedAt, sma50, sma200. Used when the feed cannot give an average | yes |
| us_screen | latest | weekly US candidate screen | US only |

**US feed document (us_feed/latest):**

```json

```

**US screen document (us_screen/latest):** date, fetchedAt, source, sectors (the ETF tickers screened) and stocks, a list where each stock carries sym, sector, weight, date, close, sma50, sma200, ema20, atr14, high50, high1, low10, low3, r1m, avgVol, adv (average dollar volume), volRatio, chg52, earnings (next results date or empty) and flags.

**Trade document fields (app v9):** status (planned, open, closed), createdDate, stock, setup, sector, industry, sectorRank, regime, pivot, trigger, limit, method (gtt or amo), stop0, stop, atr, resultsDate, riskPct, oneR, fullShares, firstShares, addShares, pilot, checksFailed[], note, lots[], sells[], added, thirdSold, extSold, gttPlaced; later also maxClose, minClose and lastEval {date, close}, which feed MAE and MFE. These are close-based, not intraday, so they understate how often a stop was nearly hit.

Field lists above were read from the live documents and the app code on 3 Oct 2026. Types and allowed values (for example the exact values of status) will be formalised as a JSON schema file in build phase 3, and a test will compare every saved document with it.

## Settings and configuration

**Today (app v9):** rule values live in constants near the top of the app script. Changing a rule means editing the script, which is the thing the target design removes.

| Constant | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| SETUPS | Per setup: trigger %, limit %, max stop width, basis text, stop hint, flags (breakout, ipo, resultsExempt) |
| LIMITS (India), LIMITS_US | Per regime: allowed setups, number of top sectors, risk per trade %, max positions, and cap (the maximum total open risk for new trades as a % of capital, not a position cap; to be renamed maxOpenRiskPct in the rewrite). Red setups must change to pilots only in v10 (Engine Rules OQ-8) |
| SECTORS, SECTORS_US | Sector names and the index or ETF used for each |
| IDX | Benchmark names per market (US: SPY, QQQ; India: Nifty 50, Nifty 500) |
| EXIT_RULES | Exit rule names recorded in the journal |
| SCR_MIN_ADV, SCR_MIN_RESULTS | US screen liquidity floor ($50 million) and results-date gap (10 trading days) |

**Target:** one settings file per market (settings/india.json, settings/us.json) holding every value above plus the room multiple (3R in both markets, C-112), the 1.5 ATR stop floor, distribution-day and breadth thresholds, VIX threshold, liquidity floors and the source list. Both files share one schema (settings/schema.json), so a value that exists for one market must exist for the other, even when equal. The app and the scripts read the same files. Each file carries a rulesVersion field that must match the current Engine Rules version; a mismatch fails the build and is shown on the screen footer.

**Secrets:** none in the app. The target alert tokens live in GitHub repository secrets. Logged exception to the no-API-key rule (owner decision, 3 Oct 2026): US end-of-day data may use Tiingo as the primary source, Massive (the former Polygon) or EODHD as the backup, and FRED for a VIX cross-check (FRED lags a day; Cboe's free VIX history file needs no key and is the candidate primary VIX source, pending the seven-day test), each key held only as a GitHub repository secret (TIINGO_KEY, POLYGON_KEY, EODHD_KEY, FRED_KEY), never in the repo, the app or the data files. The India feed stays keyless. The Alpha Vantage key stays unused. A key is adopted for production only after the seven-day source test shows the free plan returns 200 or more days of history and its newest SPY close agrees with the second source within 0.1%. The EMA length is 20 everywhere: the feed field is ema20 and the screen computes a 20-period EMA. The app code still names a local variable ema21, a leftover to rename in the rewrite.

## Target repository layout

This layout is a proposal for the GitHub build, to be confirmed in build phase 0. It keeps rules, data, scripts and app apart.

```text

```

**Actual layout so far (3 Oct 2026), where it differs from the target above:** TypeScript on Node 22 with type stripping and no dependencies, not a separate language per layer. The engine is `src/engine/` (indicators, regime, sectors, setups, sizing, checklist, exits, journal, book, legacy, proposals, format, settings) and is pure functions with no I/O. Tests are in `test/`. `fixtures/` holds the market files from the live database (`db/`), the v9 a`nd v9.1 app files (app/, with test/app-parity.test.ts checking v9.1 against the engine`), the golden outputs of v9's own code (`expected/`) and the scheduled-task prompts (`scheduled-tasks/`). `tools/` holds the golden generators, `scripts/` the source test, alert sender and privacy check, `docs/review-notes/` one review note per engine block. Rule values are still in code (`setups.ts`); the switches and parameters for rules that are still Proposed (C-29 to C-34) are in `src/engine/settings.ts`, all off. The two source-of-truth docs are copied into the repo as docs/ENGINE_RULES.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (exported from the live docs with tools/doc-xml-to-md.mjs). The live docs stay the source of truth: after any change to either doc, re-export the copy and commit it in the same step; a test fails if the rules version in the code and in the copy differ. Nothing personal (capital, holdings, trades) is in the repo; a test blocks it from `data/` and `fixtures/db/`.

The two docs stay the master copies. A job in the repo fails if docs/ENGINE_RULES.md carries a different rules version from settings/*.json.

## Testing, runbook and failure handling

**Testing today:** the US screen was tested with a headless browser against seeded data (test_ui.js checks the panel renders; test_plan.js checks that Plan this trade fills the New trade form for a stock). Calculations were checked against stored closes. There is no automated test of the India path.

**Testing target:** unit tests for every function in the engine using fixtures from real days; a replay test that feeds a saved run through the engine and compares the regime, the ranking and the screen with saved answers; a data-health test per source; any change to a rule value fails the tests until the Engine Rules version is bumped.

**Testing progress (3 Oct 2026):** 98 tests pass in CI on every push. Seven engine blocks are replayed against the original v9 code run over seeded random inputs (regime, sector ranking, sizing, checklist, exits, journal, book and legacy numbers), plus tests that quote the rule text and, for Proposed rules, hand-built cases. A replay proves the port equals v9, not that v9's rules are right. Still to do: replay the engine over stored real days once the source test has produced them (Gate B), and the ten-session parallel run per market (Gate A).

**Runbook, when something looks wrong:**

1. Check the as-of dates on the feed. A stale date means the fill did not run or the source did not update.
2. Check the run log of the failing job (today the task's run history; target the Actions run) for a 403, 407 or 429. Those mean blocked or rate limited: follow hard rule 4 and record it in the quirks list.
3. Compare one sector's computed 200 SMA with the stored closes count. Fewer than 200 dates means the value is a fallback and flagged.
4. If a value is wrong and the source is right, fix the compute step and add a test with that day's data.
5. If the source is wrong, add or change an override, log it, and open a Change log entry if a rule has to change.

**Failure handling:** a failed run keeps the previous good data and raises a flag; it never writes zeros or guesses. Today, tasks have no self-healing and nobody is alerted. The target sends a Telegram or ntfy alert on any failed or stale run.

**Checked on 3 Oct 2026:** the India feed is dated 1 Oct, which is right because 2 Oct was a holiday and 3 Oct is a Saturday. The US feed holds 2 Oct data, written at 07:25 IST on 3 Oct, so the morning run worked. The India nightly run of 1 Oct finished in about 40 seconds and the feed carries flags that some stocks have stale EMAs (Dhan technical page) and two prices came from an earlier run, so that run may have under-fetched; this is open item OQ-6 in the Engine Rules. Five US sectors still use TipRanks 200 SMAs with stale stamps until the history top-up completes.

## Handover checklist and glossary

**Before handing this to a person or an AI tool:**

- [ ] Both documents are current: the Engine Rules version matches the code, and the Change log has every decision to date.
- [ ] The open items in the Engine Rules (OQ-5, OQ-6, OQ-7, OQ-8) are closed or assigned.
- [ ] The schema is formalised as a JSON schema file and a test checks saved documents against it (field lists are written out in this document today).
- [ ] The repo layout above is built and the tests pass.
- [ ] Every data source has been run from the real runner (GitHub servers) and its status in the sources table is current.
- [ ] Scheduled jobs, alert channels and where secrets are kept are listed with who owns each.
- [ ] The new owner has run the runbook once on a deliberately stale feed.

**For an AI coding tool:** give it both documents, the repo, and the instruction to change a rule only by writing the Change log row first and to update the tests with the change.

**Glossary:**

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| R, 1R | The money risked on a trade, the distance from entry to stop times shares |
| ATR | Average true range, the typical daily price swing, here over 14 sessions |
| SMA, EMA | Simple and exponential moving averages, for example 50 SMA, 20 EMA |
| Regime, traffic light | Green, Yellow or Red market state that sets how much risk is allowed |
| Distribution day | A day the index falls on higher volume, a sign of selling |
| Follow-through day | A strong up-day on rising volume after a correction, a sign of recovery |
| Setup | A named pattern for entering a stock (base breakout, pullbacks, earnings gap) |
| Pivot | The price above which a base breaks out |
| Persistence | A sector holding a top rank on two consecutive weekends |
| MAE, MFE | Worst and best points of a trade versus entry, in R |
| Feed | The data the fill jobs write for the app to read |
| Source of truth | The one document or file that wins when copies disagree |
| Pilot | A trade at reduced risk (0.25%) in a Red market, an early sector or a new leader |
| GTT, AMO | India broker orders: a standing trigger order, and an after-market order placed for the next morning |
| RS, RS leader | Relative strength against the market; a leader is in the top 20% (India) or has its RS line rising against SPY (US) |
| Legacy book | The owner's older India holdings, managed by an exit test and a separate risk budget, not by the new-trade rules |
| Bhavcopy | NSE's daily file of every listed stock's prices and volume |

## Decisions to make before the build

Added after the first review on 3 Oct 2026. Each one changes the design if it goes the other way, so settle them before phase 1.

| # | Decision | Why it matters | Recommendation | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Source test from the real runner (phase 0) | NSE may block cloud servers, and several sources were rejected only because of the Claude fetch tool or the organisation proxy, not the source. Yahoo chart, stooq and Tiingo's free tier are untested from GitHub | A throwaway workflow calls every candidate source daily for a week and logs the status code. If NSE blocks GitHub, India runs on a small VPS or a cron on the owner's own machine | India runner decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner): GitHub, reviewed on Sat 10 Oct from the week's log (scripts/summarise-source-test.mjs prints the verdict). Success means HTTP 200 and the file's internal date (dataDate) equals the session date, because NSE has served the previous session under a new day's filename; a 200 with a stale date is a failure. Switch to a small server or the owner's machine if any one of these holds: (1) on any weekday the index-close file was not fetched with the right date by 23:00 IST, which leaves one more poll before the 23:30 deadline; (2) any single weekday where every NSE probe returned 403 or 429 (a full-day block); (3) 403 or 429 on two or more different days (intermittent). Two isolated 429s on different days at the first probe of the window, with success later in the same window, are normal for NSE and do not trigger a switch by themselves. The IST time the file first appears with the right date is logged each day and sets the production polling window. The choice is cheap to reverse: the scripts are plain Node with no dependencies and run unchanged from any scheduler. No rule changes, so nothing in the Engine Rules. Status of the test (3 Oct 2026): probes run from GitHub every 30 minutes on weekdays; first full week is Mon 5 to Fri 9 Oct, summary due Sat 10 Oct. GitHub stays the India runner unless that week shows blocks, and the week must include at least one successful fetch of the index-close file inside the nightly window, because the regime depends on it and it has not yet been observed from GitHub. First result: NSE bhavcopy, event calendar and Nifty 500 list answered 200; Yahoo chart returned 429; Stooq 403 |
| 2 | Hosting and privacy | GitHub Pages is public on the free plan, so committed data would publish holdings, capital and trades | Keep personal data out of any public repo: private repo with Cloudflare Pages behind a login, or a local app | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner): private repo on the free GitHub plan, so Pages cannot serve it. Recommended: Cloudflare Pages behind a free login (Cloudflare Access), deployed from the private repo. Confirmed by owner 3 Oct 2026 |
| 3 | Where trades and journal persist | Browser storage is lost with the browser profile, and the fresh-money test depends on the journal | Commit trades through the GitHub API to a private repo, or use a small hosted database | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner): closed trades and the journal are committed to the private repo through the GitHub API; browser storage is only a cache |
| 4 | One language for the engine | If the app is JavaScript and the jobs are Python, two engines drift apart | Write the engine in TypeScript, run the nightly jobs in Node, and import the same module in the app | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner) |
| 5 | India breadth | Today breadth is a manual scan feeding tracker.b, so the regime depends on a number typed each night | Store the NSE daily bhavcopy (whole-market closes) and compute breadth and the whole-market scan from it; build this store first | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner) |
| 6 | Corporate actions for single stocks | Unadjusted closes are right for index ETFs but wrong across a split or bonus, which breaks a stock's 200 SMA and 52-week high for a year | Use the NSE corporate actions file to adjust or flag; set the maximum unexplained daily move in phase 1 | Open |
| 7 | Correcting a bad close | Never overwriting a stored date means one bad fetch is permanent | Allow a logged, flagged re-fetch of a named date | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner) |
| 8 | Market calendars | Skipped days for expiry, rebalancing, holidays and Muhurat need a source | A holiday and special-day file per market in settings, updated yearly, used by the tests | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner) |
| 9 | Fixtures | The Claude runtime holds the only copy of the data and the v9 script | Before any build, export every collection and the v9 script into the repo as the first test fixtures | Done 3 Oct 2026: fixtures/ in the private repo. Market and regime collections, the v9 app file and the three task prompts are committed; capital, legacy, trades, logs, overrides and holdings-keyed fields are deliberately not |
| 10 | Data-health numbers | Checks without numbers cannot block anything | Set maximum daily move, minimum stored dates and maximum staleness per source in phase 1 | Open |
| 11 | Nightly schedule | GitHub's timer is best-effort and can run 10 to 40 minutes late, and the NSE file's publication time varies | The job polls every 20 minutes inside a window until the file appears, then stops. Phase 0 logs the publication time daily, in IST. Owner approved 3 Oct 2026: polling stops at 23:30 IST, and if the file never appeared the alert names which file is missing and says whether the previous session's file is still being served under today's date (the probe already detects that) | Recommended |
| 12 | Alert heartbeat | Alerts only on failure mean a dead alert channel looks like a quiet week | Send one message a week saying the desk is alive | Recommended |
| 13 | Closes basis | The documents said both unadjusted and split-adjusted | Split-adjusted and dividend-unadjusted closes in both markets, with a one-time re-baseline of the stored US history and a test. This refines the earlier statement that closes are unadjusted | Recommended |
| 14 | Archive constituent lists | Without past membership, backtests carry survivorship bias | Save the index and ETF constituent lists nightly from phase 1; it is a few kilobytes a day | Recommended |

The build phases and what each delivers are in the scope of work document. Each phase there has a deliverable and a definition of done.
