# How a stock is shortlisted: India and US (brief for review)

Status as at 11 Oct 2026, version 5 (after four outside reviews the same day). Source: `docs/ENGINE_RULES.md` (rules) and `src/ingest/us-screen.ts` (the US code). Sections 1 to 3 describe what exists; sections 4 to 9 are proposals and change nothing until the test in section 7 is run and the owner signs off. Review history and probe results are in the appendices.

## 1. The funnel, both markets

1. **Market regime** (Green, Yellow or Red) from index distribution days, breadth, follow-through day and VIX. It decides which setups are allowed, how many sectors are tradable and how much risk per trade (section 5).
2. **Sector gate and rank.** A sector passes if its 3-month return beats the benchmark's 3-month return and it closes above its 50-day average (in Red, only the 3-month test). Score = 2 x 3-month return + 1-month return. Top 4 pass (top 2 in Yellow). A sector must be in the top 4 on two consecutive weekends for full size; a new leader trades as a pilot only. Above the 200-day average is "confirmed", below is "early" (pilot only). Maximum 2 open positions per industry and 3 per sector.
3. **Stock screen** inside the passing sectors (sections 2 and 3).
4. **Setup and entry check** on each stock that passes (section 5).
5. **Trade checklist** (the 60-second check): RS leader, stop at a chart level and at least 1.5 x ATR away, size from the risk formula, cap 20% of capital, at most 2 new entries a day, highest RS first. One failed item means skip.

## 2. US: live today, run weekly (Saturday)

**Pool.** The top 10 holdings of each ETF in the passing sectors (equities only; a stock under two ETFs is kept once). Data: Tiingo split-adjusted bars; earnings date from StockAnalysis.

| Test | Rule |
|---|---|
| Trend | Close above 50-day and 200-day averages, and 50-day above 200-day |
| Leads its sector | 1-month return at least equal to its sector ETF's |
| Liquidity | Average daily dollar volume of $50 million or more |
| Results | Next results date more than 10 trading days away; unknown is flagged, never passed |
| Setup and room | A setup allowed in this regime is in place, stop width within the setup's limit, and at least 3R of room to the 50-day high |
| Freshness | Data dated before the screen date is excluded |

**Ready** = every test passes. **Watch** = trend, liquidity and results pass but no setup, room, stop width or relative strength. Setups used in the US: base breakout (1), IPO base (1ipo), 20 EMA pullback (2, Green only), 50 SMA pullback (4). The earnings-gap setup (3) is not used in the US.

## 3. India: manual today (Chartink), nothing automated

The sector gate and ranking already run from the official NSE index file. The stock scan is typed in by hand from Chartink using the trend template:

- Close above the 150-day and 200-day averages; 150-day above 200-day; 200-day rising versus a month ago.
- 50-day above the 150-day and 200-day; close above the 50-day.
- At least 30% above the 52-week low and within 25% of the 52-week high.
- Traded value over Rs 10 crore a day; price over Rs 50; market cap over Rs 1,000 crore.

Then the same setup, stop, room (3R, as in the US; C-112) and results-date checks as the US. Setup 3 (earnings gap) is allowed in India. India VIX above 20 halves risk per trade. The RS-leader test for India is: top 20% of the Nifty 500 on 3- or 6-month return.

## 4. Proposed in outline (change C-20, not built): one whole-market nightly scan

Apply one trend template to every liquid listed stock each night in both markets, with a relative-strength percentile rank, instead of the US ETF-holdings pool and the manual India scan. Liquidity floors differ by market. The data for India is already stored (daily NSE file with adjusted averages). Purpose: find smaller stocks outside the sector indexes.

## 5. Differences between the two markets today

| | US (live) | India (manual) |
|---|---|---|
| Universe | Top 10 holdings of passing sector ETFs | Whole market, market cap over Rs 1,000 crore |
| Trend tests | Close above 50 and 200; 50 above 200 | The same plus 150-day, 200-day rising, 30% above 52-week low, within 25% of 52-week high |
| High and low used | 50-session | 52-week |
| Relative strength | 1-month return versus sector ETF; RS line versus SPY checked by eye | Top 20% of Nifty 500 on 3 or 6 months |
| Liquidity | $50 million a day | Rs 10 crore a day |
| Room to resistance | 3R | 3R (C-112) |
| Setups | 1, 1ipo, 2, 4 | 1, 1ipo, 2, 3, 4 |
| Max positions (Green) | 4 | 10 |


## 6. Proposed rule set (version 5, after reviews 1 to 4)

Principle: buy the strongest stocks in a healthy market. The evidence is strongest for relative-strength momentum and for trading near 52-week highs; both can fail in sharp rebounds after a bear market, which the regime filter limits. Chart-pattern tests are trader practice with little formal evidence, so they are tested before adoption. All thresholds below are **fixed before the replay and not tuned** (section 7).

**The universe, each night, in both markets**
- **India:** the **top 750 NSE cash-segment (EQ series) stocks by trailing six-month median traded value, recomputed monthly from the daily NSE file.** This replaces the index-list idea: the Nifty Total Market index only launched on 13 October 2021 and its press release gives index values, not pre-launch constituent lists (checked 11 Oct), and NSE publishes current constituents, not monthly point-in-time lists. The daily-file universe is point-in-time, survivorship-free and the same rule live and in the replay. **The universe size is pinned at 750** so the top-20% threshold does not move. **The rank defines the universe; there is no separate rupee floor** (a floor could shrink the universe and move the threshold). The replay reports the traded value of the 750th name each month. A stock with at least 65 sessions of history enters the ranking using its median over the history available, so a recent listing is not shut out by the six-month window.
- **India exclusions:** stocks under ASM or GSM surveillance, in the trade-for-trade segment, or on a **2% or 5% price band** (10% and wider, and no-band, stay). A stop cannot execute through a locked circuit. Listing source named at build. Historical ASM, GSM and band lists may not be reconstructible, in which case the replay universe is wider than the live one and the result is labelled flattered.
- **US:** the **top 1,500 common stocks by 20-day dollar volume, universe size pinned at 1,500** (so the top-20% threshold does not float), with a **$10 million a day floor as a safety net, a single number, and a $10 minimum price**. Minimum listing age 65 sessions. **Source: Massive (formerly Polygon) grouped daily, free plan, no cost (section 9).** Common stocks are selected with Massive's tickers reference endpoint (type field), refreshed monthly and stored with its as-of date, so a past universe is built from the list as it stood (reviewer's claim that this endpoint is free on our plan is unverified; checked at build). **Histories are keyed on the composite FIGI, or broken at the delisting date, so a reissued ticker never splices two companies into one series.**
- **Liquidity:** India price over Rs 50 (no separate traded-value floor); US as above. One binding rule: **the planned position is at most about 1% of the stock's 20-day average traded value**, stated against the current swing capital so it moves when the Portfolio Manager changes it.

**The screen**
1. **Relative-strength score:** weighted return over the last year, 40, 20, 20, 20 across the four quarters (latest first). Percentile rank on the pinned liquid universe. **Gate and first sort key:** top 20%. The skip-the-last-month variant (12-1) is logged as a diagnostic.
2. **One trend template, 52 weeks, both markets:** close above the 50-, 150- and 200-day averages; 150-day above 200-day; 200-day rising versus a month ago; 50-day above 150-day; at least 30% above the 52-week low; within 25% of the 52-week high. **A filter, not a ranking input.**
3. **Industry strength:** median relative strength of liquid members, **minimum five members**, falling back to the sector score below that. India classification: NSE's basic-industry field. US: a sub-industry map is needed and the price source does not supply one; source to be named at build. The sector gate (score 2 x 3-month + 1-month, so one-month momentum is kept at industry level) and the two-week persistence rule stay as the market-level filter.
4. **Base quality at scan time, thresholds frozen:** tight = ATR over 10 sessions below 0.7 of ATR over 50; distance to the pivot within 5%.
5. **Not extended, frozen:** more than 25% above the 50-day average is extended and skipped.
6. **Breakout volume** (at least 150% of the 50-day average) is an **entry-day check**, not a scan test.
7. **Ranked output:** a fixed composite, relative-strength percentile carrying most of the weight, then base tightness, then distance to the pivot; ties by relative strength; weights logged in settings before the replay. **Top 10 shown, at most 3 per industry**, so the list shows the next-best outside a crowded theme.
8. **Shortlist in every regime.** In Red the Watch list is still produced, ready for a follow-through day.

**Rule clarifications**
- **Room, defined mechanically.** Overhead resistance = the **highest high of the prior 250 sessions, if it is above the pivot**; if not, there is none and the test is waived. Room is the distance from entry to that level, at least 3R (US) or 2R (India). **The replay reports how many template passers that are not at highs this test removes;** if it removes most of them, the test is doing the template's job twice and the pre-registered fix is 2R in both markets (an owner decision, since the US 3R reflects the tax drag), not a looser resistance definition. The nearest swing-high resistance the trader types into the checklist at entry stays as the discretionary check; the scan uses the mechanical one so two implementations agree. The test therefore bites on stocks that are 10 to 25% below their highs.
- **IPO base (setup 1ipo).** The anchor lock-in runs from the allotment date and SEBI's 2022 rule locks 50% of anchor shares for 30 days and the rest for 90, so the rule is **at least 95 calendar days since allotment**. Our data holds the listing date, not the allotment date, so it is applied as **at least 100 calendar days since listing** (about 69 sessions), which clears the 90-day unlock under both the T+3 and the older T+6 listing timetables. A **formed base** is at least **15 sessions**, **depth no more than 25% from the base high**, and the **pivot within 5% of the base high** (so 15 sessions of decline does not qualify). Flag the six-month pre-IPO shareholder unlock in India and the typical 180-day insider lock-up in the US. The US general minimum listing age stays at 65 sessions.
- **US one-month lead over the sector ETF:** a flag on the shortlist, shown and not buried, never a gate.
- **Kept as they are:** regime filter, results-date test (more than 10 trading days; unknown is flagged, never passed; India dates from NSE board-meeting announcements), stop-width limits, setups per regime, sizing, the daily cap.
- **Left out for now:** earnings-growth and fundamentals screens.


## 7. Test plan (version 5)

**What is replayed.** Three versions: **A** today's rules, **codified** (for India, the Chartink template written as code, an approximation of what was done by hand, not an exact replay); **B** relative-strength gate, one template, ranked output, pinned universe (rules 1, 2, 3, 7); **C** B plus base quality and the extension limit (rules 4, 5). No further versions; the thresholds inside them are frozen in section 6. **Tested hierarchically: B is compared with A first; C is evaluated only if B passes, and the question C answers is whether base quality and the extension limit add to B.** This keeps the false-pass rate at the stated level (two parallel 90% tests would give roughly one in five).

**Two stages, kept apart.** (1) Pick quality: forward returns of each version's picks at **20 and 60 sessions** against the liquid universe and the index, with no setups, stops or exits. (2) Whole funnel: the same picks through setups, stops and exits with costs (the Portfolio Manager's charges model plus slippage that rises for thinner names).

**Data prerequisites.**
- **Corporate actions for the whole universe**, 2020 to 2025, back-filled before any replay (not just held names): an unadjusted split corrupts the trend template, and the Swing Desk store starts in October 2025.
- **NSE changed the daily-file format in 2024** (date to verify); the loader reads both layouts.
- **US:** Massive keeps delisted names on past dates (probe, appendix B), so the US replay is not survivorship-biased on that evidence; it covers about two years only (section 9). **One US price source for screen, stops and engine** (decision below), or a daily reconciliation with a stated tolerance; two closes for one stock on days the vendors disagree are not allowed.
- **India data load is weeks of work, not a switch.** NSE's archive is free but hostile to automation (cookies, headers, rate limits, blocks): a throttled, resumable job for 2020 to 2025, expected to be re-run. The corporate-action history (NSE corporate-actions CSV) is the larger piece. The India test is possible at no cost; it is **not ready**.

**Pre-registered criterion (version 4).** Two conditions, each with an external anchor, so nobody picks a number.
- **Primary comparison:** the picks B (or C) makes that A does not (the symmetric difference), out of sample (2024 to 2026), because A's picks are largely a subset of B's and the shared names contribute nothing to the difference.
- **Statistical condition:** the **block-bootstrap 90% interval on the mean 20-session excess return** of those picks (over the liquid universe) **excludes zero**.
- **Economic condition:** the point estimate **exceeds the extra cost of trading the difference**. When the daily entry cap binds, the symmetric-difference picks are trades B makes instead of A's trades, so the bar is the cost *difference* (charges model plus slippage for the thinner tier, less the cost of the A trade displaced), not the full round trip. When the cap does not bind (the extra picks are additional trades), the full round trip of the median pick applies. Which case holds is stated in the replay report.
- **Also reported:** median and hit rate; the sign of the difference in each half-year from 2024-H1 to 2026-H1 as a consistency report. "3 of 5 half-years" is dropped as a pass condition, because five coin flips give three the same sign more often than not; if a per-period condition is wanted, 4 of 5 is the weakest that means anything.
- **Sample size:** no judgement before about 300 non-overlapping picks per version per market; overlapping windows and shared names reduce the effective number.
- **Forward test read date, fixed now.** The forward log (section 9) is read once, after **300 non-overlapping picks per version or twelve months of logging, whichever is later**, with the section 7 criterion. At the US weekly cadence (a handful of names) this is likely more than a year; nobody reads it earlier because it looks good. C's candidates are logged beside A's and B's from the same night.
- **If neither B nor C passes, A stays.** The 2020 to 2023 window is for fitting and diagnostics only.

**Diagnostics, not extra versions:**
- B's rules run on A's US ETF-holdings pool ("B-narrow"). If B-narrow beats A the rules help; if only the wide-universe B does, the gain is the universe, where slippage and lock-ups live.
- B's picks split by whether the last month was their strongest quarter.
- Picks tagged by whether the sector was in the top 4 and whether the pick came through the bottom-up path.
- **Rebound check:** B's and C's results in the 60 sessions after every Red-to-Green transition (March to June 2020, November 2020, April 2025). If they lose to A there, the regime filter, not the screen, needs work.


## 8. Change management

C-20 is split in two:
- **C-20a: whole-market nightly scan infrastructure.** No rule change; a wider candidate list shown alongside today's. Needs the corporate-action back-fill and the daily-file loader. Can be built now.
- **C-20b: the rule changes in section 6.** Adopted only after the section 7 criterion passes.
- **Order of work:** (0) back-fill the free Massive window (section 9), before anything else; (1) C-20a infrastructure; (2) replay; (3) sign-off on C-20b.

## 9. Data plan and no-spend evidence standard (owner decision, 11 Oct 2026: no paid plans, no money spent)

**US source: Massive free plan, grouped daily endpoint.** One call returns every US stock for one date; the free plan serves about two years and the window rolls forward every day. The existing `POLYGON_KEY` secret works (appendix B). Tiingo's free plan (500 symbols a month) cannot supply a whole-market history; no paid plan is bought.

**Back-fill now (time-sensitive).** Every day not fetched is lost for good once it leaves the two-year window. About 500 grouped-day calls at 5 a minute is under two hours of workflow time, roughly 110 Actions minutes (the dashboard projects 1,243 of 2,000 for the month against a 1,400 target, so this one-off sits close to the target). Run first, store the result, then the nightly call extends it.

**Storage: all common stocks, every day, 4 to 5 fields.** Close, high, low, volume, dollar volume or VWAP, for about 11,000 rows a day, gzipped to well under 100 KB a day: a year is under 30 MB and the repo can hold it. The top-1,500 ranking needs 20-day volume for every candidate before the cut, and a stock that enters the universe next month needs its history today. A 3,000-name cut would throw away the names C-20 exists to find. Raw files (1.3 MB a day) are not stored.

**Evidence standard.**
- **India:** the full section 7 test, at no cost, once the NSE load is done.
- **US:** the free window (about Nov 2024 to now: one correction, otherwise bull market) cannot meet the sample-size and regime requirements. The US replay is a **consistency check, not a decision test**: B or C is adopted for the US only if it passes in India and the US replay shows the same sign and does not contradict it. The B-narrow diagnostic still runs over the free two years.
- **Forward test (free):** from the day the nightly scan runs, every night's shortlist (ticker, rank, trigger) is stored in the repo and scored on 20- and 60-session forward returns as they mature, with A, B and C logged side by side. Read date fixed in section 7. This is the real US decision.
- **Nightly US scan:** one call a day on the existing key; Actions minutes are measured before it is switched on.

**Owner sign-offs outstanding.** (1) The no-spend evidence standard above. (2) Sections 6 and 7 as modified. (3) The nightly US job on the free key. (4) Starting the back-fill now. Nothing else is built until these are answered.

---

# Appendix A. Review history (11 Oct 2026; decisions are in sections 6 to 9)

## A1. Review 1 (11 Oct 2026): answers to the seven questions

1. One template for both markets: yes; the US omissions come from the ETF-holdings pool. 52 weeks in both.
2. Sector first or stock alone: keep the sector gate in B; answer from the replay tags.
3. Relative strength: both gate and first sort key; percentile on the liquid universe only.
4. US one-month lead: replace with the weighted percentile; keep the one-month comparison as a flag.
5. India data: drop market cap; superseded in review 2 by the daily-file top-750 universe.
6. Ranking: a fixed, pre-registered composite; volume as an entry-day check.
7. Liquidity floors: Rs 10 crore and Rs 50 fine for India with the 1% rule; US floor down to $10 to 20 million with a $10 minimum.

## A2. Review 2 (11 Oct 2026): what was accepted and what was not

**Accepted:** the out-of-sample pass criterion and the symmetric-difference comparison; bootstrap intervals; mean and hit rate beside the median; the derived margin; the bhavcopy top-750 universe (the index-list idea fails on history); corporate-action back-fill for the whole universe; the two daily-file layouts; the B-narrow diagnostic; the 65-session IPO minimum (40 sessions fell between the 30- and 90-day unlocks); frozen thresholds in C; the rebound check; the 3-per-industry cap on the top 10; the mechanical room definition; the pinned universe size and the 12-1 diagnostic; the five-member minimum for industry medians; excluding 2% and 5% price bands only; the 300-pick sample size; the 65-session US listing minimum.

**Checked by me:** the Nifty Total Market launch date and its press-release contents (13 October 2021; index values, not earlier constituent lists). **Not checked by me:** the SEBI anchor lock-in rule (cited by the reviewer from law-firm notes), the 2024 daily-file format change, the momentum literature, and the claim that Tiingo's delisted-ticker coverage decides US survivorship.

**One simplification to flag:** the mechanical room test uses the 52-week high as overhead resistance, which is the farthest level, not the nearest swing high. It is reproducible; the trader's own nearest-resistance check at entry covers the nearer levels.

**Still for the owner to sign off:** see section 11.

## A3. Review 3 (11 Oct 2026): the three sign-offs, each with one modification

The reviewer's recommendation was to sign off all three, but none as written. The modified versions are in sections 6 and 7.

1. **The pass margin.** Principle kept (derived, not chosen); the method changed, because "set from the dispersion of A's own picks" was still a free choice. It is replaced by a bootstrap condition and an economic condition anchored to trading cost (section 7). "3 of 5 half-years" is dropped as a pass condition.
2. **The IPO minimum.** The 65 sessions and the 15-session base stand, restated in calendar days from allotment (at least 95) because that is what the rule protects against; applied as at least 100 days from listing, since our data has the listing date. The base is defined by depth (at most 25%) and pivot position (within 5% of the base high). **A departure from the reviewer's wording:** the reviewer wrote 95 days from allotment; I apply 100 days from listing because the allotment date is not in our data, and say so.
3. **The US liquidity floor.** $10 million, one number (not a range, which becomes a tuning knob), with the US universe pinned at the top 1,500 by 20-day dollar volume so the percentile does not float.

**Four conflicts found in version 3 and fixed:**
- The six-month median traded value kept every recent IPO out of the universe while setup 1ipo needs one. Fixed: a stock enters once it has 65 sessions, using its history so far.
- A Rs 10 crore floor and a pinned 750 could disagree. Fixed: the rank defines the India universe and the floor is dropped; the 750th name's traded value is reported monthly.
- The mechanical room test would pass mainly at new highs. A diagnostic and a pre-registered fallback (2R in both markets) were added.
- Items marked "not checked": the anchor lock-in is in SEBI's ICDR (Amendment) Regulations 2022, effective 1 April 2022, amending Schedule XIII; the reviewer's law-firm notes summarise it and the gazette is the primary source. The 2024 daily-file format change (NSE's move to the common UDiFF file, per the reviewer's recollection) stays marked "to verify" until the loader is written against a real file from each side of the change.

**For the owner:** approve sections 6 and 7 as modified, or say what to change. Nothing is built until you do. Open check: whether the data plan can supply 1,500 US tickers a day.

## A4. Review 4 (11 Oct 2026): accepted

All points accepted and folded into sections 6 to 9:
- Back-fill the free Massive window first; store all common stocks per day, 4 to 5 fields.
- Common-stock filter from the tickers reference endpoint with an as-of date; break histories at ticker reuse (FIGI or delisting date).
- Section 6 US universe rewritten from Tiingo to 1,500 on Massive; one US price source or a daily reconciliation tolerance.
- Test B before C (hierarchical), so the error rate holds without a wider interval.
- Economic condition on the cost difference, not the absolute cost. **Nuance added:** the difference applies when the daily cap binds; otherwise the full round trip.
- Forward-test read date pre-registered (300 non-overlapping picks per version or twelve months, whichever is later).
- India data load stated as weeks of work; section 7 heading corrected; document restructured into decisions plus appendices.
- Reviewer's assessments kept: US evidence standard honest; three delisted names say "not obviously survivorship-biased", not "clean"; adjusted flag sufficient for the template and RS score; IPO rule in calendar days is robust.
- **Not verified by me:** that the tickers reference endpoint is free on our plan.

# Appendix B. Probe results and data-plan facts

**Data plan facts (11 Oct):** Tiingo Starter (free) 50 requests an hour, 1,000 a day, 500 unique symbols a month, 1 GB bandwidth; Power $30 a month, 10,000 an hour, 100,000 a day, 110,247 symbols a month, 40 GB; both with 30+ years of end-of-day history. The existing US jobs (about 40 screen stocks, sector ETFs, daily tickers) already use part of the free 500-symbol monthly allowance. Source: Tiingo's pricing page, read 11 Oct; the live key's own plan and usage were not visible to me.

**Alternative US sources (checked 11 Oct from the vendors' pricing and documentation pages):**
- **Massive (formerly Polygon), grouped daily endpoint:** one request returns open, high, low, close, volume and VWAP for **all US stocks on one date**, with an `adjusted` switch for splits. Free Basic plan: 5 calls a minute, 2 years of history, end-of-day data. Starter $29 a month: unlimited calls, 5 years of history. Developer $79 a month: 10 years. Records exist back to 2003 but each plan limits how far back it serves. A past date returns whoever traded that day, so it is point-in-time by construction; delisted-ticker coverage is **not stated on the page (to verify)**, as is how split adjustment behaves for old dates. The free plan is enough for the nightly scan (one call a day; about 260 calls to build a year of history); the full 2020 to 2026 test needs the $79 Developer plan for one month (the 5-year Starter plan reaches only back to late 2021).
- **EODHD, bulk end-of-day API:** one exchange for one date per request, flat 100 calls; also splits and dividends in bulk. The free plan has no bulk (20 calls a day). The $19.99 plan has 100,000 calls a day, but the page lists bulk only under higher plans, so whether $19.99 includes it is **unclear (to verify with support)**; delisted coverage is not stated.
- **Tiingo** has no bulk end-of-day file (per-ticker only).

**The Massive key is already in use (confirmed 11 Oct from the stored probe log, `data/source-test/log.ndjson`, run 10 Oct).** The repo's `POLYGON_KEY` secret exists and works on the current plan: the grouped daily call for 9 Oct 2026 returned 12,598 US rows in one request (status 200, 0.5 seconds, 1.3 MB, unadjusted), and its SPY close (778.57) matched Tiingo's exactly. A 400-day SPY history call returned 276 sessions. Not yet tested: the 2-year history limit on the free plan in practice, the delisted-ticker coverage of past dates, and the adjusted-price behaviour for old dates (the probe used unadjusted prices).

**Massive probe results (run 11 Oct 2026, `data/source-test/massive-probe.json`; script `probes/probe-massive.mjs`, workflow `probe-massive`):**
1. **History depth on the free plan: about two years, as advertised.** Grouped daily bars were served for 10 Oct 2025, 11 Apr 2025 and 8 Nov 2024 (10,676 rows) and refused (HTTP 403, "past historical entitlements") for 11 Sep 2024, 12 Oct 2023, 12 Oct 2021 and 16 Mar 2020. So the free plan cannot serve the 2020 to 2023 fitting window.
2. **Delisted names are present on past dates.** WBA, JNPR and ANSS (all delisted in 2025) appear on 4 Mar 2025 and are absent on 9 Oct 2026, while AAPL appears on both. Past dates are point-in-time, so the US replay is not survivorship-biased on this evidence (three names checked, not a full audit).
3. **Split adjustment works on old dates.** For ORLY (15-for-1, effective 10 Jun 2025), the 6 Jun 2025 close is 1,377.72 raw and 91.848 adjusted, a ratio of exactly 15; the splits endpoint returns the same split. Dividend adjustment was not tested.
4. **A grouped day holds about 11,000 to 12,600 rows**, including ETFs and other non-common securities; the universe step must filter to common stocks (and ETFs where wanted) before ranking.
5. **Still needed for the full test:** the Developer plan ($79 for one month, 10 years of history) for 2020 to 2023; the free plan covers late 2024 onward.

# IND-BASE-1: the simple momentum baseline on six years of India history (C-54), written 17 Oct 2026 before any run

Status: CONFIRMED 17 Oct 2026 by the owner. Nothing has been run at the time of this commit. Numbers marked (analyst) become fixed when this file is committed with "CONFIRMED" below; any change after a run voids the run. Source: the external review of 17 Oct 2026 (test the design against its simplest evidenced version, add a holding-period curve, India first).

## Why
The US replays covered one year and could not tell a rule from luck. India has six years of daily history in the repo (Jan 2020 to Oct 2025, two full cycles) and an as-of data view that applies corporate actions only as they were known. The first question is not about the Swing Desk's pattern layer; it is whether plain relative-strength momentum, with an index filter, earns anything on this data after cost. That is the yardstick the full funnel must later beat. The India scan is not built, so the funnel comparison is a later test (it needs its own entry in this log once the scan exists).

## What is tested
1. **Baseline.** Each month, rank the eligible stocks on 12-1 momentum and hold the top decile, equal weight, in cash when the index is below its 200-day average.
2. **Holding curve.** For the same monthly top-decile picks, the net return and the excess over the eligible universe at 20, 60 and 120 sessions after entry.

## Definitions (all fixed now; no parameter is searched, sweep size 0)
- **Data.** data/india/bhav-hist and data/india/bhav through the as-of view (src/backtest/india-asof.ts), series EQ and BE, delisted stocks included as listed on each night. Index: Nifty 500 close from data/india/idx-hist.
- **Eligible on a signal night.** Close at least Rs 20 (analyst); median traded value (close x volume) of the last 20 sessions at least Rs 5 crore (analyst); at least 260 sessions of history in the as-of view; then the 500 largest by that 20-session median traded value (analyst).
- **12-1 momentum.** Adjusted close 21 sessions ago divided by adjusted close 252 sessions ago, minus 1. Top decile of the eligible list by that figure (about 50 names).
- **Timing.** Signal at the close of the first session of each month; entry at the next session's close; hold to the entry close of the next month's signal. A name still in the top decile is held through, with no trade.
- **Regime.** If the Nifty 500 close on the signal night is below its own 200-session average, no entries that month and existing positions are sold at the next session's close.
- **Cost, round trip, by 20-session median traded value** (analyst; includes statutory charges and spread): Rs 100 crore or more 0.35%; Rs 25 crore or more 0.50%; below that 0.80%. Charged on each trade, half on entry and half on exit.
- **Benchmarks.** (a) Nifty 500 price index, buy and hold; (b) the whole eligible list, equal weight, same monthly rebalance and same costs, in the same regime rule (isolates the momentum effect from the universe).
- **Windows.** Fit: first signal Jan 2021 to Dec 2023. Holdout: Jan 2024 to Oct 2025. The holdout result is computed in the same run but written to a separate file that is not opened until the reveal is logged here; one reveal for this hypothesis.
- **Uncertainty.** Block bootstrap of the monthly net excess, 3-month blocks, 5,000 resamples, seed 20261018 (analyst), 90% interval.
- **Integrity checks (must pass or the run is void).** The as-of leak check (scripts/check-india-asof.mjs) passes; a seeded 10-night check shows the signal list rebuilt from data truncated at the night equals the list used in the run.

## Pass criteria (decided on the fit window, confirmed once on the holdout)
- **P1, momentum is present.** Mean monthly net excess of the top decile over benchmark (b) is above zero, with the bootstrap 90% interval's lower bound above zero, in the fit window; and the holdout mean is above zero.
- **P2, it beats the index.** Net excess over Nifty 500 (a) is above zero in the fit window and in the holdout, compounded.
- **P3, not a few months.** The fit-window mean excess stays above zero after the three best months are dropped.
- **P4, every calendar year reported.** Net excess by calendar year is printed; no criterion, but a single year that carries the whole result is stated as such.
- **P5, robust to cost.** P1 to P3 are recomputed with every cost doubled. A Pass is labelled "robust" only if they still hold; otherwise it is labelled "cost-sensitive" (added 17 Oct 2026 at confirmation, before any run).
- **Outcomes.** Pass: P1, P2 and P3 all hold. Fail: mean excess below zero in both windows. Anything else: inconclusive, reported as "cannot tell", with no adoption. Passing does not adopt anything; it sets the yardstick the Swing Desk funnel has to beat.

## Holding-curve rule (reported, one decision attached)
The 20, 60 and 120-session annualised net excess over the eligible universe is printed with intervals. If the 20-session figure is less than 75% of the best of the three, the horizon question goes to the owner as a finding ("swing" may be the wrong horizon for this signal); nothing changes automatically.

## Reported alongside, never used to choose
Four one-at-a-time variants of the baseline, fit window only, shown as a plateau check: no skip month; top 5%; top 20%; index filter off. A parameter taken from this table carries sweep size 5 (the baseline plus four) and does not become a rule from this test.

## Known limits
Survivorship is handled (delisted names are in); adjustment is as-of but 336 unresolved breaks in thin stocks and demergers drop history, which slightly favours liquid, clean names. No dividends in the price return (the benchmarks have none either). Costs are assumed, not measured. Six years is two cycles, not a long sample; this test can fail a rule more reliably than it can prove one.

CONFIRMED: owner, 17 Oct 2026 (definitions as written; two corrections made at confirmation before any run: sweep size stated as 5, and the double-cost label P5 added).

# US paper book: streams and read rules (C-53), written 16 Oct 2026 before any paper position

Status: CONFIRMED v2 (17 Oct 2026), after the external review of the C-52 diagnostics. Logging starts the first night after the confirmation. Source: docs/replay/US-SCAN-2-RESULT-2026-10-16.md.

## Purpose
Measure on real forward fills three questions the one-year replay cannot answer, one change at a time: does a stop sized in ATR instead of a 6 to 8% cap change the result (the width question), does a mechanical entry do as well as the pattern trigger (the entry question), and does the scan have positive expectancy in R after cost at all. Nothing here changes a live rule or places a real order.

## Candidates
The nightly top-10 list of US-SCAN-1 (Ready and Watch, composite order, 3 per industry), frozen. Names more than 25% above the 50-day are skipped in every stream (the extension rule stays). Setup allowances follow the regime light of the night (US Yellow: 1, 1ipo and 4; Green and Red: 1, 1ipo, 2 and 4) in every stream. Setup 3 is not in the scan and is not modelled.

## Shapes (the same in every stream)
- Breakout (setup 1, or 1ipo on the IPO path): price within 5% of the 50-session high; for stocks on the main path also a tight base (ATR10/ATR50 below 0.7), as in US-SCAN-1.
- 20 EMA pullback (setup 2, where allowed): close at or above the 20 EMA, a low in the last 5 sessions at or below it, close above the 50-day.
- 50-day pullback (setup 4): close at or above the 50-day, a low in the last 5 sessions at or below it.
The first shape in the order 1, 2, 4 that matches and builds under the stream's own stop rule is used (so a stream can use a later shape when an earlier one cannot be built under its rules).

## Three streams, a chain: each changes one thing from the one before
1. **Official.** The Ready list as live: buy at trigger (basis plus 0.5% for setup 1, 0.2% for 2 and 4) with the limit (1%), one session to fill (fills at the trigger if the next session's high reaches it and its low is at or under the limit). Stop at the chart level widened to 1.5 ATR14; the setup's stop-width cap (8% setup 1, 10% 1ipo, 7% setup 2, 6% setup 4) and the 3R room test (to the 250-session high, waived when none) applied.
2. **Cap-waived** (changes only the stop rule). Same shapes, triggers, limits and fills, on the whole top-10 list. Stop: the official stop (chart level, at least 1.5 ATR14 away); if that is farther than 2.5 ATR14 from the trigger, the stop is 2.5 ATR14 below the trigger and the trade is tagged "inside base". A trade whose stop would be wider than 12% of the trigger is skipped. The percent cap and the room test are not applied; trades are tagged "over cap" and "room fail" where the official rule would have skipped them.
3. **Comparator** (changes only the entry rule on top of stream 2). Same shapes, same stop rule and tags as stream 2, same candidates. Entry at the next session's close if tonight is a signal night: breakout shape, first close above the highest high of the previous 20 sessions (the previous close was not); pullback shapes, first close back above the 20-day average (setup 2) or the 50-day average (setup 4) after a close below it in the last 5 sessions. The stop is placed with the stream-2 rule from tonight's close and re-measured at the actual entry; skipped if the stop is then wider than 12%.
Cap-waived against official answers the width question; comparator against cap-waived answers the entry question.

## Exits (all streams)
The exit rules at daily-close resolution: the stop fills at the stop; rule 3 (failed breakout within 3 sessions), 4 (time stop, 10 sessions without a close at +1R), 5 (sell a third at +2R, stop to entry), 6 (trail: first close below the 20 EMA in weeks 1 to 7, a weekly close below the 10-week average from week 8) and 7 (sell a third at 20% above the 20 EMA) act at the next session's close; rule 9 (regime light drops: stops on trades below +1R move to the higher of the day's low and the 10 EMA, never above the close); rule 8 is not modelled because no results dates are held, and every trade says so. A trade closes at the latest after 60 sessions.

## What every trade records
Stream, setup, group, regime at entry, signal date, entry date, trigger, fill, stop in percent and in ATR14 units, ATR14 as a percent of price, room in R, tags (over cap, room fail, inside base), the 20-day dollar volume and the cost tier (0.20% round trip from $100M a day, 0.35% from $25M, 0.60% from $10M), exit date, exit reason (stop, stop at entry, failed breakout, time stop, trail, extended third, max hold) and the result in R after cost. No portfolio limits or sizing are applied: every trade stands alone in R.

## Read rules (fixed now)
- Top-10 forward log: read at 300 non-overlapping picks or 12 months, whichever is later, as already decided.
- The three trade streams are read at 12 months from the first logged night regardless of count, with each stream's trade count reported (the official stream may never reach 300, and that is itself a result). A first look at 150 trades in a stream is allowed and judged on nothing.
- Official: expectancy in R after cost above zero, 90% block-bootstrap interval (blocks of 5 entry nights, 5,000 resamples) excluding zero.
- Width: cap-waived against official, and the over-cap trades of stream 2 on their own, same interval rule on the difference or the trades.
- Entry: comparator against cap-waived on trades that share a candidate, same interval rule; if the mechanical entry does as well, the pattern trigger is cost without benefit and the scan becomes a watch list with one mechanical entry.
- Reported, not judged: results by regime at entry, by ATR-percent tercile (the question whether the edge lives in the calmer half of the universe is asked at read time, never made a rule now), by group, setup, tag and cost tier, win rate, exit reasons, and the read without any group above 25% of a stream's trades.

## Known items recorded now
- The India engine uses the same 1.5 ATR floor and the same style of chart-level stops, in a market at least as volatile; the same tension (percentage caps against a very volatile universe) will appear when the India scan is built.
- A backtester module (one implementation shared with the engine, as-of data, run manifests committed before each run, fit and holdout windows, standard outputs and sensitivity curves) is planned after the India history load; see docs/SCOPE.md. It is for pre-registered tests and plateau checks, not for searching parameters.

## Limits
Fills from highs and lows only (no opens), so gaps past the limit are approximated; no earnings dates; no portfolio limits; shadow streams are not live rules; the stock list is whatever the nightly feed carried, so the paper book has no survivorship bias.

CONFIRMED: owner, 17 Oct 2026 (v2 definitions as written above; engine commit 20e2d7b; logging starts the next US nightly run).

# US-SCAN-2: changes and test criteria (C-52), written 16 Oct 2026 before any run

Status: CONFIRMED 16 Oct 2026 by the owner. Nothing has been built or run at the time of this commit. Numbers marked (analyst) become fixed when this file is committed with "CONFIRMED" below; any change after a run voids the run. Source of the three changes: external review of 16 Oct 2026 of the C-51 replay result.

## Why
The C-51 replay could not run its pre-registered test: Ready names appeared 11 times in 229 nights (the tight-base gate almost never passes). On the top-10 fallback, 76 of 330 picks came from Metal mining at +3.7%; the other 254 averaged -0.33%. So the first version found one group's rally and nothing else. This year has now been seen, so US-SCAN-2 is a reasoned set of changes, not a fit, and the forward log decides regardless.

## The three changes (everything else stays as US-SCAN-1: universe, RS 40/20/20/20, template, group rule, weights 60/25/15, setups, hysteresis)
1. **Tightness leaves the gate and stays in the score.** ATR10/ATR50 below 0.7 is no longer required. The 25% tightness weight stays and orders candidates. (The structural base test, a 15-session pause no more than 20% deep, is NOT added: one change, not both.) The 5% pivot limit still decides whether a trigger exists.
2. **Regime light from history.** The live regime rules (src/engine/regime.ts) are run unchanged over the stored history, so each night uses the light that was known that night. Where VIX history cannot be fetched, the light is run without it and labelled.
3. **Rolling group cap.** No more than 4 new picks from one group in any 20 sessions (analyst), on top of the 3 per industry per night. Excess candidates are skipped in composite order.

## Replay
Same 229 nights, same pick rules as C-51 (entry next close, 20-session hold, non-overlapping). Two changes to the measurement, not the rules: (a) cost by 20-day dollar volume, round trip: 0.20% at $100M or more, 0.35% from $25M to $100M, 0.60% from $10M to $25M (analyst); (b) every result is also shown excluding the single group with the most pick return in that run.
Stage 2 (second test): the same picks run through trigger fills, the 1.5-ATR stop, the time stop and the trail from the exit rules, measured in R after the tiered cost. Fills assumed at the trigger when the next session's high reaches it, at the limit at worst.

## Pass criteria (the judged set is the names with a setup, "Ready" under change 1)
1. At least 150 non-overlapping picks. If fewer, the test is "not executable" and nothing else is claimed.
2. Leak test as in C-51 (10 seeded nights, seed 20261016).
3. Edge: 90% block-bootstrap interval of mean 20-session excess over SPY, after tiered cost, excludes zero on the whole set AND on the set without its top group.
4. Stability: positive in both halves of the period.
5. Control: above the 95th percentile of 200 matched random controls (same cost rule, seed 20261016).
6. Concentration: no group above 25% of picks.
7. Stage 2: at least 150 trades, mean R after tiered cost above zero, 90% interval excluding zero.

## Reported, not judged
Each change alone (three ablations), per-group share of picks, 12-1 diagnostic beside 40/20/20/20, SPY above and below its 200-day average, picks per night, hit rate, worst pick, and the same measure for the weekly screen's 38 names (today's holdings over past dates, so it flatters that screen; a rough guide only).

## Decision rule
All seven pass: US-SCAN-2 becomes the frozen configuration and a new forward clock starts; the forward log and a paper book (at least 150 closed trades, positive R after tiered cost) still decide any live use. Any fails: record which, change nothing on this data, and take the next step with the owner.

## Known limits
Same as C-51: today's stock list leaves out delisted names (true numbers are lower), one year is one market, no earnings-date check. This year has been seen, which is why criterion 3 requires the result without its top group.

CONFIRMED: owner, 16 Oct 2026 (cap of 4 and the cost tiers stand as the analyst's figures).

# US scan historical replay: pass criteria (C-51), written 16 Oct 2026 before any run

Status: CONFIRMED 16 Oct 2026 (owner: "keep" on the 150-pick minimum; the 0.30% cost stays as the analyst's figure because the owner has not supplied a different one). Nothing has been run at the time of this commit. Any change after a run makes the run void.

## What is replayed
- The scan exactly as frozen in US-SCAN-1 (src/ingest/us-scan-settings.ts at commit 0cd8f9d). No setting is changed or tuned in this run. A different setting would be a separate, logged run.
- Every stored night from the first night with 252 sessions of history (needed for the four-quarter relative strength) up to 20 sessions before the last stored day. About 230 nights (Oct 2025 to Sep 2026).
- Data: data/us/grouped, tickers-2026-10-12.json, splits.json, sic.json.
- Regime light: no history is stored. Headline run uses Yellow on every night (2 groups). A second run with Green (4 groups) is reported as a sensitivity, not judged.

## Picks
- A (headline): every name on the Ready list (setup defined) on a night. B (secondary): every name in the top-10 composite list, Ready or Watch.
- Entry: the close of the next session after the name appears. Exit: the close 20 sessions later. (Trigger fills and the nine exit rules are phase 2, not this run.)
- Non-overlapping: a ticker is counted once per 20 sessions after its entry.
- Cost: 0.30% of price per round trip (analyst), deducted from every pick.
- Benchmark: SPY over the same 20 sessions. Excess = pick return after cost minus SPY return.

## Pass criteria (all on pick set A, Yellow run)
1. Enough picks: at least 150 non-overlapping picks. If fewer, the replay is "not evaluable" for A and criterion 3 is judged on B instead, labelled so.
2. Method check (leak test): for 10 nights drawn at random (seed 20261016), the scan run on data truncated at that night gives the same Ready list and ranks as the run on the full data, for every stock with no split after that night. Any other difference fails the run.
3. Edge: the block-bootstrap 90% interval of the mean 20-session excess (blocks of 5 entry nights, 5,000 resamples, seed 20261016) excludes zero, and the point estimate is positive.
4. Stability: the point estimate is positive in both halves of the period (earlier half, later half).
5. Control: the mean excess of the picks is above the 95th percentile of 200 matched random controls (each control: the same nights, the same number of names per night, drawn at random from names that pass the price, dollar-volume and 65-session floors, same entry and exit, same cost). Seed 20261016.

## Reported, not judged
The same results with a 0.60% round-trip cost (sensitivity, because the owner's real cost is unconfirmed). Results by market type (SPY above or below its 200-day average at entry), by group, by the 12-1 and 6-month diagnostics, composite weights 60/25/15 against 100/0/0, hit rate, worst pick, and the number of picks per night.

## Known limits (stated now, not discovered later)
- The stock list is today's reference file, so names delisted before 12 Oct 2026 are missing (survivorship). The results will look better than live.
- One year of testable nights is one market. A pass here is evidence, not proof; the forward log and paper book continue.
- No earnings-date check, dividends or trigger fills are modelled in phase 1.

## Decision rule
All five criteria pass: record "replay supports the scan" and move to phase 2 (exit rules, trigger fills). Any fails: record which, do not tune on this data, and decide with the owner what to change; any change restarts the forward clock.

CONFIRMED: owner, 16 Oct 2026 (150 picks kept; 0.30% cost stands, with a 0.60% sensitivity reported).

# IND-BASE-1 result, fit window (C-54), 17 Oct 2026

Pre-registration: docs/replay/IND-BASE-1-PREREG.md (confirmed 17 Oct 2026 before any run). Run: scripts/backtest-ind-base1.mjs on commit of this file. The holdout (Jan 2024 to Sep 2025 returns) was computed in the same run, written to data/replay/ind-base1-holdout.json and not read before this fit result was committed. Integrity checks passed: the as-of leak check (10 nights) and the seeded 10-night signal rebuild from truncated data (identical lists, picks and regime). A first run that never invested (the regime flag was read from the wrong list, found because the filter-off variant did invest) was discarded before any result was read; it changed nothing in the pre-registration.

## Fit window: signals Jan 2021 to Dec 2023 (36 months, 29 invested, 7 in cash)
| | Strategy (top decile, filter on) | Eligible list, same rule | Nifty 500 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compounded | +150.9% | +74.8% | +66.1% |
| 2021 | +77.8% | +42.7% | +31.0% |
| 2022 | -10.1% | -9.3% | +1.6% |
| 2023 | +57.0% | +35.0% | +24.8% |

Mean monthly net return 2.77%. Mean monthly excess over the eligible list 1.10%, bootstrap 90% interval 0.12% to 2.08%. Excess over Nifty 500, compounded, +84.9 points. Mean excess after dropping the three best months 0.59%.

**P1, P2, P3 all hold in the fit window. At double cost they still hold** (mean excess 0.98%, interval 0.01% to 1.95%, +64.4 points over Nifty 500, 0.48% after dropping three months), but the double-cost lower bound is barely above zero.

## Reported, not used to choose (one at a time, fit window)
Mean excess over the eligible list / compounded return: no skip month 0.89% / +132%; top 5% 1.33% / +170%; top 20% 0.68% / +118%; filter off 1.18% / +202%. The result is positive in every variant; the filter-off run has the highest return because 2022 and early 2023 were weak but not a collapse in this universe.

## Holding curve, fit window (invested months, picks against the eligible list, net of a round trip, annualised excess with 90% interval)
20 sessions +17.6% (4.8% to 30.6%); 60 sessions +14.8% (2.6% to 27.2%); 120 sessions +12.3% (3.5% to 20.5%). The 20-session figure is the highest, so the horizon flag does not fire. The three are not independent (overlapping picks).

## What was checked in the data
The largest name-months are real, well-known moves (TTML, NDTV, JWL, ADANITRANS), none coincides with a resolved split or bonus, and the worst are the Adani collapse, so losses are not being hidden. Median name-month gross return 1.4% against a mean of 3.7%: the mean is carried by a skewed tail. Many winners trade only Rs 7 to 20 crore a day, where the 0.80% cost tier and real fills matter most. 6 positions lost their price before exit (valued at the last close); 10 names had no entry price and were skipped; no unresolved demerger inside a hold. Two ETF-like symbols among 2,832 picks.

## Holdout reveal (one reveal, 17 Oct 2026, committed after the fit result): signals Jan 2024 to Sep 2025, 21 months
| | Strategy | Eligible list, same rule | Nifty 500 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compounded | +10.1% | +12.1% | +18.6% |
| 2024 | +37.8% | +25.4% | +17.5% |
| 2025 (to Sep) | -20.2% | -10.6% | +0.9% |

Mean monthly net return 0.71%. Mean monthly excess over the eligible list +0.04% (essentially zero). Excess over Nifty 500, compounded, -8.5 points.

Holding curve, holdout, annualised excess over the eligible list with 90% interval: 20 sessions +4.0% (-10.2% to +17.6%); 60 sessions +2.6% (-7.5% to +12.7%); 120 sessions +1.8% (-4.7% to +9.0%). Every interval includes zero.

## Against the pre-registered rule
- **P1** (mean excess above zero with a positive lower bound in the fit window, and holdout mean above zero): holds on the letter (holdout +0.04%), with no practical margin. At double cost it fails (holdout mean below zero).
- **P2** (beats Nifty 500 in both windows): holds in the fit window, **fails in the holdout** (-8.5 points).
- **P3** (survives dropping the best three months): holds.
- **P5** (double cost): P1 fails in the holdout, so even a pass would have been labelled cost-sensitive.
- **Outcome: inconclusive ("cannot tell"). Not a Pass, because P2 fails. Not a Fail, because the fit-window excess is positive.** Nothing is adopted.

## Reading it
Momentum with an index filter beat both benchmarks decisively in 2021 to 2023 and gave all of it back in the holdout: in 2025 the top decile fell 20% while the index was flat and the whole eligible list fell 11%. In 2024 and 2025 large caps led and the broad list itself trailed Nifty 500 (+12.1% against +18.6%), so the small and mid-cap tilt that carried the fit window reversed. The index filter did not help in 2025: the index stayed above its 200-day average while momentum names fell. The baseline is therefore real in some regimes and not a free lunch; it is cyclical with the small-cap cycle. Six years and one reversal is not enough to say whether the holdout is noise or a regime change; the 21-month interval on every holding horizon includes zero.

## What it means for the next steps
The yardstick the funnel has to beat is not a stable one. A longer history with more cycles is now the most useful single addition (NSE's older files back to about 2010, which adds 2013 to 2019 including the 2015 to 2016 and 2018 corrections), before any funnel comparison.

# US-SCAN-2 replay result (C-52), run 16 Oct 2026

Run as pre-registered (docs/replay/US-SCAN-2-PREREG.md, commit 146e4c7). Script: scripts/replay-us-scan2.mjs. Outputs: data/replay/us-scan2-*.json. Same 229 nights (16 Oct 2025 to 15 Sep 2026); tiered cost; regime light replayed with the live rules (53 Green, 163 Yellow, 13 Red nights; breadth rebuilt from the stored bars and within 0.8 points on average of the stored live breadth on the 32 days both exist).

## Formal status
The pre-registered test was NOT executable again. Criterion 1 failed (52 picks with a setup, 150 needed) and criterion 7 failed (19 stage-2 trades, 150 needed). Removing the tight-base gate lifted Ready names from 11 to 43 (gate change alone) or 52 (all three changes), still far short. The numbers below are exploratory.

## Criteria, v2 (all three changes), judged set = names with a setup
1. At least 150 picks: FAIL (52).
2. Leak test: PASS (10 of 10 nights identical).
3. Edge over SPY after tiered cost: FAIL. Mean +0.51%, 90% interval -2.3% to +3.5%. Without Metal mining (45 picks): -1.07%, interval -3.0% to +0.75%.
4. Positive in both halves: FAIL. Earlier +4.5%, later -2.0%.
5. Beats random control: FAIL. +0.51% against a 95th percentile of +1.96%.
6. No group above 25% of picks: PASS (largest 17%).
7. Stage 2 (exit rules in R): FAIL. 19 trades, mean -0.19 R, interval -0.52 to +0.15. Win rate 37%. Exits: 11 failed breakouts, 3 stops, 3 trail, 2 time stops.

## Each change alone (top-10 list and Ready names, mean 20-session excess, 90% interval)
| Version | Ready picks | Ready mean | Top-10 picks | Top-10 mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| US-SCAN-1, tiered cost | 11 | +0.76% | 330 | +0.66% (-1.8 to +3.2) |
| Gate only | 43 | +1.45% | 345 | +0.62% |
| Regime only | 22 | +3.61% | 388 | +1.12% |
| Cap only | 11 | +0.76% | 330 | +0.66% |
| All three (v2) | 52 | +0.51% | 401 | +1.01% (-1.5 to +3.5) |
Every interval includes zero. The cap alone changes nothing for Ready names (they never reach 4 per group in 20 sessions); it is applied to Ready names only.

## Other reported items
- Top-10 list, v2: top group by pick return is Semiconductors and components (118 picks, +2.3%) then Metal mining (76, +3.6%); without Semiconductors the other 283 picks average +0.45%.
- SPY above its 200-day average at entry: Ready 50 picks +0.45%, top-10 371 picks +1.53%. Below: 2 and 30 picks (too few; the top-10 below-200 picks average -5.4%).
- 12-1 month momentum diagnostic, Ready names: above the median +0.54% (22), below -0.05% (26).
- Regime: 13 Red nights and 53 Green nights in the year, so the fixed-Yellow runs of C-51 were a mixture.
- NOT run: the weekly-screen comparison on the same window. Its past holdings are not stored, so it would only be today's 38 names, which flatters that screen; no clean version exists.

## What it says
Removing the gate was not enough: Ready names are still rare because a setup also needs a price within 5% of the pivot (setup 1), a pullback to the average (2, 4), a stop inside the width limits and 3R of room. Only 19 of 52 Ready names got a fill on the next session, and 11 of those 19 failed back below the pivot within three sessions. The edge that exists is still concentrated (Metal mining, Semiconductors) and fades in the later half. No tuning on this data. The replay cannot support US-SCAN-2 and cannot reject the scan as a watch list.

## Limits
Delisted names are missing (flatters results); one year; stage 2 fills at the stop and next close without opens, rules 8 and 9 not modelled; fewer than 150 picks so no interval here is tight.

## Addendum: where candidates drop out of the setup layer (16 Oct 2026, after the external review)
Counts only, no returns (scripts/funnel-waterfall-us.mjs, outputs data/replay/us-funnel-waterfall-*.json). Candidate-nights summed over 228 nights, Yellow light, stocks that passed steps 1 to 5 (7,891), each counted once at the first test it fails:

| Outcome | US-SCAN-1 (gate on) | Gate off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extended (more than 25% above the 50-day) | 2,293 | 2,293 |
| No setup geometry (not within 5% of the pivot, no pullback to the 20 EMA or 50-day) | 4,190 | 2,511 |
| Stop wider than the setup's limit (6 to 8%) | 1,341 | 2,890 |
| Fails the 3R room test | 32 | 36 |
| Gets a setup | 35 | 161 |

The room test is not the choke: at 2R it frees about 10 more candidate-nights out of 7,891. The tests that remove candidates are extension, setup geometry and, with the gate off, the stop-width limit (1.5 ATR on momentum leaders is often wider than 6 to 8%). The setup order checks width before room, so room is only ever tested on candidates that already passed width; even so, a 2R room rule would change almost nothing here. No rule changed. Whether the stop-width limits suit stocks this volatile is a rule question for the owner and the reviewer, not something to tune on this year.

Fill model: stage 2 already filled at the trigger when the next session's high reached it, within the limit. Only stage 1 enters at the next close, by design, to measure pick quality without a fill model. The stage-2 fills use highs and lows only (no opens), so a gap above the limit is approximated by the limit test against the day's low.

## Addendum 2: independent tests and stop widths (16 Oct 2026)
scripts/funnel-detail-us.mjs, data/replay/us-funnel-detail-yellow-gateoff.json. Gate off, Yellow, 228 nights; 5,598 candidate-nights that passed steps 1 to 5 and were not extended. Every test is evaluated on its own (not first-failure). Stop distance is the setup's own rule (chart level, widened to 1.5 ATR14), as a percent of the trigger and in ATR14 units. These are the live rules' numbers, nothing is changed.

| Shape | Candidate-nights | Stop width 10th / median / 90th | In ATR | Over the 6-8% cap | Fails 3R room |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base breakout (within 5% of the 50-session high) | 1,999 | 8.6% / 13.8% / 21.6% | 2.6 / 3.6 / 5.1 | 1,848 (92%) | 86 (room waived when no overhead) |
| Pullback to the 20 EMA (not allowed in Yellow) | 3,027 | 6.6% / 10.8% / 17.5% | 1.5 / 2.1 / 3.3 | 2,643 (87%) | 2,461 |
| Pullback to the 50-day | 1,331 | 7.6% / 12.4% / 20.0% | 1.5 / 2.1 / 3.4 | 1,298 (98%) | 1,215 |

- The candidates are very volatile: median ATR14 is 5.1% of price (10th to 90th: 3.2% to 8.5%). A 1.5 ATR stop alone is about 7.6%, already at or past every cap (6 to 8%). So the cap is mismatched to the universe, not set a little too tight.
- Shapes are not rare: breakout only 794, 20 EMA pullback only 1,101, 50-day pullback only 376, more than one 1,927, none 1,400. The earlier "no setup shape" count was partly setups not allowed in Yellow (US Yellow allows 1, 1ipo, 3 and 4 only).
- Room will bind once the cap goes: for pullbacks 3R of a wide R fails for 81 to 91% of shapes (median room 0.6R to 1.0R). The reviewer's expectation holds here, though not at the earlier waterfall's ordering.
- A stop of up to 2.5 ATR with a 12% backstop (reviewer's proposal, counted not adopted): 1,782 candidate-nights qualify with room ignored, 203 with the 3R room test applied (against 161 today). Breakout stops sit at a median of 3.6 ATR, so most breakouts still exceed 2.5 ATR.

# US scan replay result (C-51), run 16 Oct 2026

Run exactly as pre-registered (docs/replay/US-SCAN-REPLAY-PREREG.md, commit bacb1e4). Script: scripts/replay-us-scan.mjs. Outputs: data/replay/us-scan-replay-*.json. 229 nights, 16 Oct 2025 to 15 Sep 2026, US-SCAN-1 unchanged, 20-session hold, 0.30% round-trip cost, SPY benchmark.

## Criteria (headline run: Yellow, weights 60/25/15)
1. Enough picks: FAIL. Ready names gave 11 non-overlapping picks (needed 150). Judged on the top-10 list (set B, 330 picks) as pre-registered, labelled the weaker test.
2. Leak test: PASS. 10 seeded nights, no differences. (A side finding: a full-data build that applies splits dated after the night does change the list on some nights, for example 27 and 29 Oct 2025, through the $10 price floor and cross-sectional ranks. The replay uses the real-time build, which matches a past-splits-only build on all 10 nights.)
3. Edge: FAIL. Mean 20-session excess over SPY after cost +0.60%; 90% interval -1.86% to +3.12%, includes zero.
4. Both halves positive: FAIL. Earlier half +3.2%, later half -1.8%.
5. Beats random control: PASS. Picks +0.60% against a control 95th percentile of +0.14%.

FORMAL STATUS (corrected after external review): the pre-registered test was not executable, because criterion 1 failed. Criteria 2 to 5 above were read on the top-10 list as a fallback, so they are an exploratory result. It does not support the scan as designed. No tuning on this data.

Ex-top-group check: Metal mining gave 76 of the 330 picks at +3.7% (about 280 points of pick return against 197 for the whole set). The other 254 picks average -0.33%. The year's result is one group, which also explains most of the earlier-half/later-half gap. An ex-top-group line is now a standing part of every replay.

## Reported, not judged
- Ready (set A): 11 picks in 229 nights (0.05 a night), mean excess +0.75%, hit rate 45%, worst -11.2%. Too few to read anything. The base test (ATR10/ATR50 below 0.7 with the pivot within 5%) is almost never met.
- Top-10 list (set B): 1.4 picks a night, hit rate 48%, worst pick -44.8%. SPY above its 200-day average at entry: 314 picks, +0.71%. Below: 16 picks, -1.55%.
- Cost sensitivity: at 0.60% round trip, set B mean +0.30%.
- Green run (4 groups): Ready 48 picks (+2.4%); set B 515 picks, +0.88%, interval -1.36% to +3.19%, earlier +2.9%, later -1.1%.
- Weights 100/0/0: set B 205 picks, -0.57%, earlier +5.2%, later -5.7%. Not better than 60/25/15.
- Largest groups in B: Semiconductors and components 106 picks (+0.5%), Metal mining 76 (+3.7%), Communications equipment 44 (-0.3%), Computer hardware 30 (-1.2%).

## Limits
Today's reference list leaves out delisted names (flatters results). One year is one market, and the regime light was fixed rather than historical. Entry at the next close, no trigger fills, no exit rules, no earnings check.
